339	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
340	
341	*Revised 2026-09-21 by D-015, before any review: the CAN-level detail (arbitration IDs,
342	broadcast frames, a listen-only flag, the port-traffic check) went with the MCP2515.*
343	
344	**Decision.** The capture daemon gets its signals by sending **standard OBD2 Mode 01
345	requests** through the OBD2 adapter (D-019) on a fixed, rate-limited, round-robin schedule,
346	one request outstanding at a time. Every timeout and every unanswered PID is logged.
347	
348	**Why.** D-011 (now D-024) makes this a plug-in device, and the thing that makes a plug-in
349	device work on a car it has never seen is the part of the protocol every car must speak:
350	Mode 01 is mandatory on US cars from model year 1996. *"Learns this car's normal"* is
351	precisely what lets one device serve different cars without per-model decode work: it
352	never needs to know what normal *is* ahead of time.
353	
354	**Sample-rate consequence.** Signals are round-robined, so each PID is sampled at
355	(request rate ÷ PID count) — on the order of 1 Hz each for a ~10 requests/s budget over
356	~8 PIDs. That is ample for what we watch (warm-up over minutes, fuel trim against load,
357	drift over days) and must be stated in `docs/DESIGN.md` §4. The request budget itself
358	is a design-doc number to justify, not a constant to pick.
359	
360	**Cost.** The device sends requests to the car's ECU. Kept safe by the rate limit, one
361	outstanding request, and only standard read-only Mode 01 requests — the same thing every
362	scan tool does.
363	
364	**Scope note.** "Works on any car" is the product's direction, not our claim. The claim is
365	E.1 (D-021): one car, a learned normal, fault areas named, measured error rates.
366	
367	### A.8 — A real-time clock keeps wall time while the box is off ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
368	
369	`D-030` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
370	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
371	
372	**Decision.** The box gets a small real-time clock module on the Pi's I2C bus, kept
373	running by its own backup cell or capacitor while the box is off. At boot the system
374	clock is set from it. If the clock reports its time as invalid (its backup was lost),
375	that session's wall time is marked untrusted. Every record still carries `mono_ns`
376	regardless. The phone page stays read-only: it does not set the clock.
377	
378	**Why.** The Pi has no battery-backed clock, and the box has no network (`CLAUDE.md`
379	§2.3). Raspberry Pi OS's `fake-hwclock` restores the time saved at the last shutdown, so
380	the clock does not advance while the box is off, and every boot would appear to follow the
381	previous shutdown directly. The soak (D-023) must prove a 48-hour wall-clock span across
382	parked gaps, and the report's session list needs real times. Camden chose the clock
383	module, 2026-10-21, over the phone setting the time (that depends on someone opening the
384	page on every drive) and over no wall clock at all (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.2, R5).
385	
386	**Cost.**
387	
388	- One more part, on I2C (GPIO2 and GPIO3, header pins 3 and 5), drawn in the Pi interface
389	  block, and bought only after the design is signed.
390	- Its backup cell or capacitor lives in a parked car's cabin, so its temperature rating
391	  must cover that, checked against the part's datasheet (`rtcspec`).
392	- A clock that has drifted or lost its backup must be detected rather than trusted, so the
393	  boot path checks it (`rtcboot`).
394	
395	---
396	
397	## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms
398	
399	### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F only with a Pi-side sensor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
400	
401	`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
402	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
403	· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)
404	
405	*B and F declined 2026-10-21 by D-029 (§B.7), before any review: no Pi-side sensor will be
406	added, so D and E are the committed pair and the "only if" rows below no longer apply.*
407	
408	The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.
409	
410	| Mechanism | Status | Where |
411	| --- | --- | --- |
412	| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
413	| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
414	| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | declined (D-029) | — |
415	| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | declined (D-029) | — |
416	| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |
417	
418	**D.** *Power disappears every time the key turns off* (D-024). The box shuts down
419	cleanly on its supercapacitor when it can, but the bank is empty at a cold start, a
420	pulled cable beats it, and a crank dip can reset the Pi, so storage must survive a cut at
421	any instant. *(Revised 2026-10-21 by D-024; it read "we never get a clean shutdown".)*
422	Measured by cutting the Pi's own 5 V rail mid-write, after the converter so the
423	supercapacitor cannot cover it, repeatedly, and proving recovery (`expcrash`). Pulling
424	the charger no longer tests this: it triggers a clean shutdown.
425	
426	**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
427	duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
428	each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).
429	
430	**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015, D-019).** B needs an interrupt that *our*
431	design services. The adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's Bluetooth and RFCOMM
432	stack; our process only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up
433	trivially — the comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a
434	*high-rate* stream; ~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under
435	contention" would be true and meaningless.
436	
437	**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
438	samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
439	that stresses the ring (F). That was board item `pisensor`; D-029 declined it.
440	
441	**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
442	process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.
443	
444	**Risk.** D and E alone meet the floor exactly. If either measurement fails, nothing is in
445	reserve. `pisensor` was that reserve, and D-029 declined it.
446	
447	### B.2 — Four processes, not one 🔒
448	
449	`D-002` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
450	
451	`obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and `supervisor` are separate processes with separate
452	address spaces, communicating over a shared-memory ring and Unix domain sockets.
453	
454	**Why.** Fault isolation is the product requirement, not an architectural preference: the
455	analysis engine is the most complex and least trustworthy component, and it must not be
456	able to take the capture path down with it. One process would be simpler and would fail
457	the thing the device exists to do.
458	
459	### B.3 — The ring refuses rather than overwrites 🔒

never that tidy, and a cleaned soak log is the artifact this course is best equipped to
notice.

## Before the graded run

Start soak-style runs at small scale from **M3**, not M4: daily drives, plus overnight
bench runs on a home charger against `obdsim` (labeled `synth`) to find leaks. Every leak
found in Week 9 is a crisis avoided in Week 14. `make soakcheck` runs a one-hour bench
miniature.

Leave margin to run the graded soak **twice**. You will want to.

549	### B.4 — The phone is a read-only window over the device's own Wi-Fi ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
550	
551	`D-013` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
552	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
553	
554	*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-028 (§B.6): the page also shows trends and downloads a report,
555	and the server-language sub-decision below is closed (C).*
556	
557	**Decision.** The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi access point — WPA2, a per-device passphrase, **no
558	upstream connection, no internet**. The owner's phone joins it and opens a status page
559	served from `src/interface/` by a supervised child process. The page shows exactly two
560	things — **status** and **current verdicts** — rendered from the same supervisor UDS verbs
561	`obdctl` uses. It holds no state, runs no analysis, and writes nothing. `obdctl` remains
562	the primary, exact interface with all five verbs. No app, no account, no cloud, and the
563	phone never pairs over Bluetooth. (The Pi itself pairs with the OBD2 adapter, D-019.)
564	
565	**Why.** The user is a car owner, not someone with a terminal in the passenger seat, so a
566	product that can only be read over SSH has no user. The handout permits it directly
567	("Serving a dashboard on the LAN is fine", §3.3; CLAUDE.md §2.1), and the device keeps
568	working with no phone present at all. It also sharpens the phone-app test: the Pi is the
569	part that is awake at every key-on; the phone is only a window onto what it already
570	recorded.
571	
572	**Why so thin.** The handout warns: *"Resist the pretty web app. A crisp CLI with five
573	query verbs and exact semantics is more defensible, and far more extensible at the
574	live-modification station."* So the page is a view, not a second interface: two screens,
575	no framework, and no number on it that `obdctl` cannot also produce. Every graded behavior
576	remains demonstrable through `obdctl` alone.
577	
578	**Cost.**
579	
580	- A network listener in the product. It binds only to the AP interface, is read-only, and
581	  lives only in `src/interface/`, where `make boundary` already allows network symbols.
582	- One more process in the 48-hour RSS plot, and Wi-Fi radio power from the box's supply
583	  (D-024).
584	- The access point shares the Pi 4's one radio chip with the Bluetooth link to the adapter
585	  (D-019). Measured by `btcoex`.
586	- **Sub-decision, closed by D-028:** the server's language. C in `src/interface/` keeps an
587	  interpreter out of the memory-stability test; Python in `ui/` is permitted by CLAUDE.md
588	  §2.5 but adds ~30 MB RSS to the soak. Recommendation: C, because the page is tiny.
589	  Camden chose C, 2026-10-21.

591	### B.6 — The phone page also downloads a report; an app is a stretch ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
592	
593	`D-028` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
594	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
595	· **Extends:** D-013 (§B.4)
596	
597	**Decision.** The status page (D-013) shows status, current verdicts and trends, and has
598	one button: **Download report**. The report is one self-contained HTML file plus a CSV of
599	the same data, generated on the box by a C program in `src/interface/`. The page still
600	writes nothing to the device. A native phone app is a stretch goal, not planned for M2 to
601	M5.
602	
603	**Report contents** (first draft; finalized in `reportspec`):
604	
605	| Section | Content |
606	| --- | --- |
607	| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy, and the mix of data sources (`live`, `replay`, `synth`), always labeled (C.2) |
608	| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
609	| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, the supercapacitor's self-check, free storage |
610	| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, the sensors that cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
611	| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
612	| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |
613	
614	**Reachability.** The box is off whenever the car is (D-024), so a phone reaches it only
615	while the car runs, or while the box is plugged into any USB-C charger at home, where it
616	boots and serves the same page.
617	
618	**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P12): the owner views data and
619	trends on a phone and downloads a report that says what is wrong with the box or the car.
620	HTML opens on any phone with no app, and the CSV lets the owner or a mechanic take the
621	numbers elsewhere. C, as D-013 recommended: the server is small, and an interpreter would
622	add tens of megabytes to the 48-hour memory plot (R3).
623	
624	**Rule kept from D-013.** The report is assembled from the same supervisor UDS verbs
625	`obdctl` uses, so every number in it can also be produced at the CLI, and every graded
626	behavior stays demonstrable through `obdctl` alone.
627	
628	**Cost.** A report generator is new code in the product: it gets rows in the failure
629	table, its memory shows in the soak plot, and the boundary check still has to show the
630	page is the only network code.
631	
632	**Alternatives rejected.** A PDF report (needs a PDF writer we would have to defend). A
633	native app (a second product to build). A Python server in `ui/` (the soak's memory).

635	### B.5 — One tri-color status light, and every live state pulses ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
636	
637	`D-027` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
638	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
639	· **Supersedes:** D-014 (§G.10)
640	
641	**Decision.** One LED, visible through the shell, shows red, yellow or green. It is
642	written **only by the supervisor** (D-014's rule, kept).
643	
644	| Light | Meaning |
645	| --- | --- |
646	| green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go |
647	| yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: riding a supply dip, or shutting down |
648	| red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** in the car; the report says which |
649	| steady yellow | Booting: held on from power-up, before the supervisor runs |
650	| any other steady light, or dark while the car runs | **Not running.** Never a valid live state |
651	| dark while the car is off | Normal: the box is off |
652	
653	Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green. Steady yellow for more
654	than about a minute means the boot never finished.
655	
656	**What counts as red.** In the box: a child down or restart-limited; the dongle silent
657	while the engine runs; storage failing or nearly full; undervoltage or thermal
658	throttling; the supercapacitor's self-check failed. In the car: a verdict has surfaced
659	after hysteresis and dwell (D.3), or a sensor the car stopped answering.
660	
661	**Why every live state pulses.** D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors: a GPIO keeps
662	its last level after the process driving it dies, so a steady green would freeze into a
663	false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If every live state blinks, a frozen light of
664	any color can only mean "not running". Camden asked for whichever pattern is safer (P11),
665	and this is.
666	
667	**The boot state.** The Pi spends roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`) booting
668	before any software can drive the light. Yellow is held on from power-up in hardware: a
669	pull keeps it lit while its GPIO is still an input, and once the supervisor drives the
670	pin, the pin wins. Camden's choice (R4). The firmware's `gpio=` setting in `config.txt`
671	might do the same with no parts; confirm on the board before relying on it.
672	
673	**Open (`ledspec`).** What the light shows after the supervisor takes the GPIOs but before
674	every child's first heartbeat. Yellow blink is taken (stored energy). Claude's
675	recommendation, not decided: the supervisor keeps yellow steady until its first
676	all-healthy check, so the light still reads "not running yet".
677	
678	**The part.** Whether yellow is its own die or red and green mixed is a part choice (two
679	GPIOs or three), made in `ledspec` from the LED's datasheet, which also sets the
680	resistors. Pins are assigned in the schematic (`schpi`).
681	
682	**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P10, P11): one light, three
683	colors, and red means an issue in either the box or the car.
684	
685	**Cost.** Two or three GPIOs instead of one; the supervisor's blink timer still must never
686	delay `waitpid` handling; the colors must stay distinguishable through the shell
687	(`enclspec`). Red merges box and car issues, so the report must say which.
688	
689	**Alternative rejected.** D-014's single-color patterns (a double-blink for a verdict): a
690	pattern code the owner has to learn.
691

693	
694	## C. Storage and data integrity
695	
696	### C.1 — Append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records 🔒
697	
698	`D-002/D` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
699	
700	*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-025 (§C.3), with Camden's explicit yes: records are written in
701	committed batches, and baselines are saved in A/B checkpoint slots. Every rule below
702	stays.*
703	
704	Records are never rewritten in place. Each carries a magic number for resynchronization
705	and a CRC32 over its whole body. Recovery scans from the last known-good offset, verifies
706	CRCs, truncates the torn tail, and logs exactly what was lost.
707	
708	**Why.** We are interrupted mid-write by design, several times a day. Rewriting in place
709	can destroy data that was previously correct; appending can only ever damage the last
710	record. The CRC is what makes a torn record *detectable* rather than merely wrong — and
711	wrong numbers you trust are more dangerous than missing numbers you know about.
712	
713	**Open sub-decision (M2, Lance):** fsync batch size and interval. There is no correct
714	value, only one justifiable from user requirements. Document the argument in `docs/DESIGN.md`
715	§4 before writing the code.
716	
717	### C.2 — Every record carries a provenance tag 🔒
718	
719	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
720	
721	Every record and every log line carries `src = live | replay | synth`. Present in the
722	format from day one, before any replay tooling exists.
723	
724	**Why.** Handout §5: replayed or synthesized data must be labeled everywhere it appears —
725	logs, report, demo. Making it a mandatory field rather than a convention means it is
726	structurally impossible to forget. Mislabeling synthesized data as live is the single
727	integrity failure this course is best equipped to detect, and the worst trade available
728	anywhere in it.
729	
730	### C.3 — Write-ahead transactions and A/B checkpoints ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
731	
732	`D-025` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session, extending 🔒 C.1) + Claude
733	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
734	· **Extends:** 🔒 C.1, whose rules all stay: append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records,
735	each carrying its `src` tag (C.2)
736	
737	**Decision.**
738	
739	- **Transactions (`storaged`).** `storaged` drains the ring into batches: a
740	  `BEGIN(txn_id)` record, the sample records, a `COMMIT(txn_id)` record, then one
741	  `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT` is on disk.
742	- **Checkpoints (`analyzed`).** `analyzed` holds the learned per-bin baselines (D-031),
743	  so it checkpoints them: now and then, a snapshot of the baselines plus the log offset
744	  and the last committed `txn_id` it covers. There are two alternating slots, A and B,
745	  each CRC'd and carrying a generation counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut never
746	  destroys the previous good one.
747	- **Recovery at boot.** `storaged` scans its log forward from the last offset it knows was
748	  committed, verifying every CRC. The scan stops at the first bad record and truncates the
749	  torn tail, and a batch with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN` (**undo**).
750	  `analyzed` then loads the newest valid checkpoint slot and re-applies every committed
751	  batch after its offset (**redo**), through the same code as live analysis. Both log
752	  exactly what was recovered and what was lost, as counts and offsets.
753	- **Every session starts with a boot record** that says whether the previous session
754	  ended in a clean shutdown or was recovered. That needs a positive marker: a clean
755	  shutdown ends the log with a shutdown record after its last `COMMIT`, because a crash
756	  just after a `COMMIT` otherwise looks exactly like a clean end.
757	
758	**Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (C.1), so there is
759	no before-image to restore: undo means discarding an uncommitted tail. Say so plainly at
760	the defense, and do not claim an undo log the design does not need.
761	
762	**Extending a locked decision.** C.1 is 🔒. Camden approved this extension explicitly in
763	the 2026-10-21 session (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P4), because it ties the storage
764	layer to the logging and checkpoint techniques taught in class. C.1 stays 🔒 and gains a
765	pointer.
766	
767	**Provisional numbers (estimates).** One `COMMIT` and one `fsync` per batch of about one
768	second of samples. Records of about 48 bytes at 10 to 20 requests a second come to about
769	1 KB/s, or about 3.5 MB per running hour. The worst loss from a power cut that beats the
770	clean shutdown is then about one second of samples. The argument for the batch size is
771	still written in `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 before the code, as C.1 requires (`fsync`).
772	
773	**Record format.** The new record kinds (transaction begin and commit, boot, clean
774	shutdown) and a boot id in the header are settled in `recfmt`. The CRC known-answer test
775	does not change.
776	
777	**Cost.** Recovery now spans two processes, so the crash tests (cut the file at every
778	byte offset, then `expcrash` on the device) must cover both. Checkpoint frequency trades
779	write load against redo time at boot.
780	
781	### C.4 — Drive captures are JSONL from a Python tool, VIN hashed ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
782	
783	`D-033` · Decided M2, 2026-10-26 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
784	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
785	
786	**Decision.** Until `obdd` exists, real-car data is collected by `tools/obdlog.py`, run on
787	Camden's Mac (or the Pi) against the OBDLink LX. It writes one file per session,
788	`data/drive-<time>-<src>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line: a `header` (adapter,
789	protocol, battery voltage, VIN hash, PID list, tool and schema version), a `sample` per
790	reply (`src`, `seq`, `t_mono`, `t_wall`, `pid`, raw hex, decoded value, unit), an `event`
791	for every non-sample outcome (`no_data`, `timeout`, `link_lost`, `reconnected`, ...),
792	optional `gps` lines and a `footer`. It polls every supported PID round-robin as fast as
793	the adapter answers. Writes are append-only and fsync'd every 50 lines or 1 s. The VIN is
794	shown on screen and stored only as the first 12 hex digits of its SHA-256. A session
795	against `obdsim` is labeled `synth` on every line, because the simulator's reset banner
796	says `SIM`.
797	
798	**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-26: the first drive must log everything the car will answer so
799	the data can be studied before the pipeline is designed around it. JSONL is readable by
800	eye and by any analysis tool; the raw hex beside the decoded value means a decoding bug
801	never costs data; event lines mean nothing is dropped silently (D-012). Camden chose
802	hashing over storing the VIN.
803	
804	**A departure from D-012, stated.** D-012 budgets about 10 requests a second on a
805	rate-limited schedule. This tool keeps D-012's one outstanding request, the core of its
806	safety argument, but sends the next request as soon as the last is answered, because the
807	first drives exist to measure what the adapter can do. The product's `obdd` keeps a rate
808	limit, set from that measurement (`canreq`).
809	
810	**What this is not.** It is not mechanism D and not the on-disk format of `storaged`
811	(`recfmt`, D-025). The product stays C (CLAUDE.md §2.4); this is a collection tool in
812	`tools/` (§2.5). `tools/replay.py` will convert these files into the product's records,
813	labeled `replay`.
814	
815	**Cost.** The hash is pseudonymization, not anonymity: a VIN has little entropy, so
816	anyone holding candidate VINs can test them. Raw logs stay out of git (`data/` is
817	ignored); only short excerpts are committed as evidence.
818	
819	### C.5 — The on-disk record format (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
820	
821	`D-034` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-26 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session, without his review
822	of the details · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜

product that can only be read over SSH has no user. The handout permits it directly

working with no phone present at all. It also sharpens the phone-app test: the Pi is the
part that is awake at every key-on; the phone is only a window onto what it already

**Why so thin.** The handout warns: *"Resist the pretty web app. A crisp CLI with five
query verbs and exact semantics is more defensible, and far more extensible at the
live-modification station."* So the page is a view, not a second interface: two screens,

**Decision.** The status page (D-013) shows status, current verdicts and trends, and has

| --- | --- |

### B.5 — One tri-color status light, and every live state pulses ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-027` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-014 (§G.10)

**Decision.** One LED, visible through the shell, shows red, yellow or green. It is
written **only by the supervisor** (D-014's rule, kept).

| Light | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go |
| yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: riding a supply dip, or shutting down |
| red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** in the car; the report says which |
| steady yellow | Booting: held on from power-up, before the supervisor runs |
| any other steady light, or dark while the car runs | **Not running.** Never a valid live state |
| dark while the car is off | Normal: the box is off |

Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green. Steady yellow for more
than about a minute means the boot never finished.

**What counts as red.** In the box: a child down or restart-limited; the dongle silent
while the engine runs; storage failing or nearly full; undervoltage or thermal
throttling; the supercapacitor's self-check failed. In the car: a verdict has surfaced
after hysteresis and dwell (D.3), or a sensor the car stopped answering.

**Why every live state pulses.** D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors: a GPIO keeps
its last level after the process driving it dies, so a steady green would freeze into a
false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If every live state blinks, a frozen light of
any color can only mean "not running". Camden asked for whichever pattern is safer (P11),
and this is.

**The boot state.** The Pi spends roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`) booting
before any software can drive the light. Yellow is held on from power-up in hardware: a
pull keeps it lit while its GPIO is still an input, and once the supervisor drives the
pin, the pin wins. Camden's choice (R4). The firmware's `gpio=` setting in `config.txt`
might do the same with no parts; confirm on the board before relying on it.

**Open (`ledspec`).** What the light shows after the supervisor takes the GPIOs but before
every child's first heartbeat. Yellow blink is taken (stored energy). Claude's
recommendation, not decided: the supervisor keeps yellow steady until its first
all-healthy check, so the light still reads "not running yet".

**The part.** Whether yellow is its own die or red and green mixed is a part choice (two
GPIOs or three), made in `ledspec` from the LED's datasheet, which also sets the
resistors. Pins are assigned in the schematic (`schpi`).

**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P10, P11): one light, three
colors, and red means an issue in either the box or the car.

**Cost.** Two or three GPIOs instead of one; the supervisor's blink timer still must never
delay `waitpid` handling; the colors must stay distinguishable through the shell
(`enclspec`). Red merges box and car issues, so the report must say which.

**Alternative rejected.** D-014's single-color patterns (a double-blink for a verdict): a
pattern code the owner has to learn.

## C. Storage and data integrity

### C.1 — Append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records 🔒

`D-002/D` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-025 (§C.3), with Camden's explicit yes: records are written in
committed batches, and baselines are saved in A/B checkpoint slots. Every rule below
stays.*

Records are never rewritten in place. Each carries a magic number for resynchronization
and a CRC32 over its whole body. Recovery scans from the last known-good offset, verifies
CRCs, truncates the torn tail, and logs exactly what was lost.

**Why.** We are interrupted mid-write by design, several times a day. Rewriting in place
can destroy data that was previously correct; appending can only ever damage the last
record. The CRC is what makes a torn record *detectable* rather than merely wrong — and
wrong numbers you trust are more dangerous than missing numbers you know about.

**Open sub-decision (M2, Lance):** fsync batch size and interval. There is no correct
value, only one justifiable from user requirements. Document the argument in `docs/DESIGN.md`
§4 before writing the code.

### C.2 — Every record carries a provenance tag 🔒

Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

Every record and every log line carries `src = live | replay | synth`. Present in the
format from day one, before any replay tooling exists.

**Why.** Handout §5: replayed or synthesized data must be labeled everywhere it appears —
logs, report, demo. Making it a mandatory field rather than a convention means it is
structurally impossible to forget. Mislabeling synthesized data as live is the single
integrity failure this course is best equipped to detect, and the worst trade available
anywhere in it.

### C.3 — Write-ahead transactions and A/B checkpoints ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-025` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session, extending 🔒 C.1) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Extends:** 🔒 C.1, whose rules all stay: append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records,
each carrying its `src` tag (C.2)

**Decision.**

- **Transactions (`storaged`).** `storaged` drains the ring into batches: a
  `BEGIN(txn_id)` record, the sample records, a `COMMIT(txn_id)` record, then one
  `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT` is on disk.
- **Checkpoints (`analyzed`).** `analyzed` holds the learned per-bin baselines (D-031),
  so it checkpoints them: now and then, a snapshot of the baselines plus the log offset
  and the last committed `txn_id` it covers. There are two alternating slots, A and B,
  each CRC'd and carrying a generation counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut never
  destroys the previous good one.
- **Recovery at boot.** `storaged` scans its log forward from the last offset it knows was
  committed, verifying every CRC. The scan stops at the first bad record and truncates the
  torn tail, and a batch with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN` (**undo**).
  `analyzed` then loads the newest valid checkpoint slot and re-applies every committed
  batch after its offset (**redo**), through the same code as live analysis. Both log
  exactly what was recovered and what was lost, as counts and offsets.
- **Every session starts with a boot record** that says whether the previous session
  ended in a clean shutdown or was recovered. That needs a positive marker: a clean
  shutdown ends the log with a shutdown record after its last `COMMIT`, because a crash
  just after a `COMMIT` otherwise looks exactly like a clean end.

**Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (C.1), so there is
no before-image to restore: undo means discarding an uncommitted tail. Say so plainly at
the defense, and do not claim an undo log the design does not need.

**Extending a locked decision.** C.1 is 🔒. Camden approved this extension explicitly in
the 2026-10-21 session (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P4), because it ties the storage
layer to the logging and checkpoint techniques taught in class. C.1 stays 🔒 and gains a
pointer.

**Provisional numbers (estimates).** One `COMMIT` and one `fsync` per batch of about one
second of samples. Records of about 48 bytes at 10 to 20 requests a second come to about
1 KB/s, or about 3.5 MB per running hour. The worst loss from a power cut that beats the
clean shutdown is then about one second of samples. The argument for the batch size is
still written in `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 before the code, as C.1 requires (`fsync`).

**Record format.** The new record kinds (transaction begin and commit, boot, clean
shutdown) and a boot id in the header are settled in `recfmt`. The CRC known-answer test
does not change.

**Cost.** Recovery now spans two processes, so the crash tests (cut the file at every
byte offset, then `expcrash` on the device) must cover both. Checkpoint frequency trades
write load against redo time at boot.

### C.4 — Drive captures are JSONL from a Python tool, VIN hashed ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-033` · Decided M2, 2026-10-26 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** Until `obdd` exists, real-car data is collected by `tools/obdlog.py`, run on
Camden's Mac (or the Pi) against the OBDLink LX. It writes one file per session,
`data/drive-<time>-<src>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line: a `header` (adapter,
protocol, battery voltage, VIN hash, PID list, tool and schema version), a `sample` per
reply (`src`, `seq`, `t_mono`, `t_wall`, `pid`, raw hex, decoded value, unit), an `event`
for every non-sample outcome (`no_data`, `timeout`, `link_lost`, `reconnected`, ...),
optional `gps` lines and a `footer`. It polls every supported PID round-robin as fast as
the adapter answers. Writes are append-only and fsync'd every 50 lines or 1 s. The VIN is
shown on screen and stored only as the first 12 hex digits of its SHA-256. A session
against `obdsim` is labeled `synth` on every line, because the simulator's reset banner
says `SIM`.

**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-26: the first drive must log everything the car will answer so
the data can be studied before the pipeline is designed around it. JSONL is readable by
eye and by any analysis tool; the raw hex beside the decoded value means a decoding bug
never costs data; event lines mean nothing is dropped silently (D-012). Camden chose
hashing over storing the VIN.

**A departure from D-012, stated.** D-012 budgets about 10 requests a second on a
rate-limited schedule. This tool keeps D-012's one outstanding request, the core of its
safety argument, but sends the next request as soon as the last is answered, because the
first drives exist to measure what the adapter can do. The product's `obdd` keeps a rate
limit, set from that measurement (`canreq`).

**What this is not.** It is not mechanism D and not the on-disk format of `storaged`
(`recfmt`, D-025). The product stays C (CLAUDE.md §2.4); this is a collection tool in
`tools/` (§2.5). `tools/replay.py` will convert these files into the product's records,
labeled `replay`.

**Cost.** The hash is pseudonymization, not anonymity: a VIN has little entropy, so
anyone holding candidate VINs can test them. Raw logs stay out of git (`data/` is
ignored); only short excerpts are committed as evidence.

If "verdict" were solid-on, a crashed supervisor would freeze the light into a false 1550 alarm, or into a false all-clear if it froze off. With blink-only states, a stuck light of 1551 either kind can only mean *not running*. This is mechanism E's principle — a recorder that 1552 dies silently has harmed its user — applied to the one output a driver actually sees. 1553 1554 **Why the supervisor, not `analyzed`.** The supervisor already knows every child's 1555 liveness (mechanism E), so it can show "degraded" when `analyzed` itself has died; a light 1556 owned by `analyzed` would show a stale verdict instead. One 1573 commit does both — resolving one question is one responsibility, however many lines it 1574 touches across this file (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3, documentation rules). 1575

## D. Intelligence and analysis ### D.1 — Self-trained model; training in Python, inference in C 🔒 `D-004` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden (confirmed with instructor) · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜ A locally-trained, self-authored model is permitted; hosted APIs and third-party pretrained weights are not. Therefore: training in `tools/train/`, weights versioned under `models/` with the training commit in the header, **inference in C in `src/analysis/`**, no network at runtime. **Why inference in C.** First and most important for the grade: the runtime path sits inside the supervised multi-process architecture, and a Python process there muddies the boundary a grader must verify in sixty seconds. Second: it removes an interpreter, a garbage collector and ~30 MB of RSS from a 48-hour memory-stability test we are graded on. **What the model is not doing.** The features are the intelligence — operating-point binning, per-bin baselines, Mahalanobis residuals, Theil–Sen trends, all hand-written. Delete the weights file and the system still produces residuals and trends; it loses only the final labeling step. That separation is deliberate and it is the answer at the defense. ### D.2 — Analysis pipeline shape 🔒 Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜ Operating-point binning (RPM × load × coolant temp) → per-bin running mean/variance → multivariate residual (Mahalanobis) → robust trend (Theil–Sen) → classifier → state machine with hysteresis and dwell. **Why binning comes first.** Comparing a cold idle to a warm cruise is a false-alarm generator. Every comparison happens inside one bin, against genuinely comparable conditions. This single step removes more false positives than anything else downstream. **Why multivariate.** The signal is the *correlation between sensors*, not any single sensor's value — fuel trim is supposed to track load. A measure of anomaly that already accounts for normal partnerships, and alarms only when a partnership breaks, is what makes this something a threshold provably cannot do (handout §3.3). ### D.3 — Hysteresis and dwell before any verdict surfaces 🔒 Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜ No verdict reaches the user until it has persisted. Trip and un-trip levels differ deliberately. **Why.** A monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged, and an unplugged monitor is worse than none because someone far away believes it is on duty. **False-positive rate is a first-class metric in `docs/EVALUATION.md`, not an afterthought.** ### D.4 — The threshold test, as a standing rule 🔒 Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜ Every diagnostic we ship must require at least two cooperating sensors to reach its conclusion. If a single threshold on a single value could produce the verdict, it is not intelligence and it does not count. **Write the reason down in `docs/DESIGN.md` when adding a diagnostic** — this is checked at the defense. --- ## E. Switched USB power also means no battery drain while parked, and it makes mechanism D's defining constraint literally true: power is cut, unannounced, at every key-off. **Alternatives rejected** (discussed 2026-09-21): splicing the bus behind the OBD2 port (the same conductors as the port pins, plus a cut harness on a daily driver); an in-line harness at the forward camera (the 2015 CR-V EX-L has none, D-007); a contactless bus clamp (receive-only, a black box); powering the Pi from OBD2 pin 16 through our own buck converter (live with the key off, and more hardware to build and defend). **Rule this imposes:** **the Pi must not brown out at crank.** The USB-C supply is rated ≥ 5.1 V / 3 A (Pi 4), and is proven by `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start, not by its label (`docs/hardware/wiring.md`). **Cost.** - No recording while the key is off — nothing happens then worth recording, but the device also cannot run overnight in a parked car. - **The OBD2 adapter itself draws from pin 16, which is live with the key off.** Its key-off current must be measured before it is left plugged in overnight. - D-006 option (c), the parked-car soak, now requires a socket that stays live in accessory plus a battery tender. - The product is "one box, one power cable, plus the dongle in the port". ### G.10 — (was B.5) One warning light, driven by the supervisor 🗑 `D-014` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜ · **Superseded 2026-10-21 by D-027 (§B.5)**: one tri-color light; the blink-only rule is kept. **Decision.** One LED on a GPIO (proposed GPIO17, header pin 11, through 330 Ω), written **only by the supervisor**. Every state in which the device is working is a *blink pattern*: | Light | Meaning | Priority | | --- | --- | --- | | fast blink (~4 Hz) | **degraded** — a child is down, the adapter silent while the engine runs, storage failing, or undervoltage | highest | | double-blink, pause | **a verdict has surfaced** (after D.3 hysteresis and dwell) — look at the phone | | | slow blink (~1 Hz) | on duty, recording, nothing to report | lowest | | **steady on or steady off** | **the device is not running.** Never a valid state. | — | **Why a light at all.** The 3 a.m. test: nobody is looking at a phone at the moment that matters. It also makes "honest reporting through our own interface" (demo movement 1) visible from across the room when a sensor is unplugged. **Why every live state blinks.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process driving it dies. If "verdict" were solid-on, a crashed supervisor would freeze the light into a false alarm, or into a false all-clear if it froze off. With blink-only states, a stuck light of either kind can only mean *not running*. This is mechanism E's principle — a recorder that dies silently has harmed its user — applied to the one output a driver actually sees. **Why the supervisor, not `analyzed`.** The supervisor already knows every child's liveness (mechanism E), so it can show "degraded" when `analyzed` itself has died; a light owned by `analyzed` would show a stale verdict instead. Verdicts reach the supervisor over the existing UDS. One writer, no GPIO contention. **Cost.** One more thing the supervisor does, and one more thing it must not block on: the blink timer must never delay `waitpid` handling. Color, brightness and placement are open (M4 enclosure). --- ## Adding a decision Append it to the right category with the next free `D-###` for citation, and fill every field. If Claude made it without a human present, it is ⚠️ **UNREVIEWED** and it goes in the Review Queue at the top — **in the same commit that implements it**, never a later one. **Closing an open question.** When a human answers a `decision` or `question` issue, the answer moves here as a 🔒 LOCKED entry citing the issue number, and the issue closes. One commit does both — resolving one question is one responsibility, however many lines it touches across this file (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3, documentation rules).

Exit code 1
# Wiring and electrical safety

The product is one box with one USB-C port and one light, plus a Bluetooth OBD2 dongle
in the car's OBD2 port (D-019, D-024). Nothing on the car is cut, spliced or pierced.

```text
  OBD2 port ──[Bluetooth OBD2 dongle]~~ RFCOMM ~~▶ Pi (/dev/rfcomm0 → /dev/obd)

  owner's USB-C charger ──USB-C──▶ [box: power block, supercapacitor] ──5 V──▶ Pi
                                        │  source-present (divided to 3.3 V) ──▶ GPIO
                                        ◀── halt-done ─────────────────────── GPIO
  Pi GPIOs ──resistors──▶ tri-color LED ──▶ GND    (the light, D-027)
  Pi I2C (GPIO2 SDA, GPIO3 SCL) ──▶ real-time clock, powered from 3.3 V   (D-030)
```

GPIO numbers for source-present, halt-done and the light are set in the schematic
(`schpi`), not here.

> **The Pi's GPIO is 3.3 V and has zero over-voltage protection.** Source-present comes
> from the 5 V USB input, so it reaches the header only through a divider; meter it
> before it is connected. Wire everything with the Pi powered off.

## OBD2 dongle → Pi (D-019)

| Item | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |

The box takes the owner's own USB-C charger. Its power block (requirements in
`docs/DECISIONS.md` §A.6):

1. sinks 5 V only (5.1 kΩ on both CC pins), behind transient and reverse-polarity
   protection and a fuse;
2. limits input current below what the source advertises, and limits inrush into the
   empty supercapacitor bank;
3. feeds the Pi from the source first and from the bank only for the gap;
4. reports source-present on a GPIO;
5. cuts the Pi's supply when the Pi signals halt-done, even if the source has returned,
   then re-enables after a short off time;
6. powers on again by itself when the source returns.

trust its label.

| Measurement | How | Feeds | Date | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Supply dip at crank | meter or scope at the charger's output | `cranklog`, the grace period | | |

an input, so a booting box shows steady yellow.

or a dark one while the car runs, means the device is not running (DECISIONS §B.5).

| Clock pin | Pi pin | Pi signal | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SDA | 3 | GPIO2 (I2C1 SDA) | |
| SCL | 5 | GPIO3 (I2C1 SCL) | |
| VCC | 1 | 3.3 V | Power it from 3.3 V, so its I2C pull-ups never put 5 V on the Pi. Meter it before connecting. |
| GND | 6 | GND | |

The part, its backup cell or capacitor, and that backup's temperature rating are chosen in
`rtcspec`.

## Bring-up order

1. Pi on the bench, dongle powered, no car: `bluetoothctl` pairs and trusts it, then
   `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1`, `ls -l /dev/obd`, and `ATZ` answers with the dongle's
   version string. Reboot once and confirm `/dev/obd` comes back without a hand.
2. Car, key to run, engine off: `0100` returns the supported-PID bitmap.
3. Car, engine running: `010C` (RPM) changes when you touch the throttle.
4. The power measurements above: the free ones first (the owner's charger with a meter,
   key off and at crank), the bank only after the power design is signed.

Measured results go in this file, dated. A step without a recorded result has not been
done (CLAUDE.md §8.4).

# Problem memo — carwatch (Camden Thomas, Lance Baron)

## The user

Our user is Lance, who drives his 2015 Honda CR-V EX-L every day and has no way to know
how it is doing between services. His car already has a sensor on nearly everything that
matters, but the only thing that ever reads them for him is the check-engine light, and it
speaks up only once something has already gone wrong. What he wants is simple: something
that knows how *his* car normally behaves and tells him when it starts acting differently,
before a small problem becomes a breakdown. We also test the same device on Camden's 2008
Subaru Forester, because it learns whichever car it is installed in.

## The problem

Every modern engine reports what it is doing through its OBD2 port: coolant temperature,
air intake, fuel trims, oxygen sensors, RPM, load and more. Nothing in the car watches those
numbers over time, however, and nothing knows what normal looks like for this particular
engine. As a result, a slowly developing fault, such as a small vacuum leak, a lazy
thermostat or a sensor going bad, can sit inside the "acceptable" range for weeks before it
crosses the one threshold that lights the dashboard. What is missing is a device that
records that data continuously, learns this car's normal, and flags strange behavior early
enough to act on it, before the check-engine light of doom puts its owner on an hour-long
bus ride.

## Why a device

The signal we are after only shows up across many drives, and it is only interpretable with
the cold starts, the short trips and the long pulls, *all* of them, not just the drives
someone remembered to open an app for. A phone app is present only for the trips its owner
thought to record, which is a biased sample of exactly the behavior we are trying to learn.
Moreover, the interesting moment is never the moment anyone is looking: it is the third cold
start of a February week, when warm-up took ninety seconds longer than it did in January,
and nobody is holding a phone then. The device, by contrast, is already in the car, awake
at key-on and recording before anyone has decided anything is wrong. Finally, the data
stays in the car, with no account, no upload and no company holding a log of everywhere
this person drove.

## The sensors

The device reads every Mode 01 sensor the car publishes through its OBD2 port, including
coolant temperature, intake air temperature, MAP, short- and long-term fuel trims, O2, RPM
and engine load. These sensors cooperate rather than merely coexist, because **no one of
them means anything alone.** Fuel trim, for example, is only interpretable against load,
and coolant temperature only points at the cooling system once ambient temperature and load
have been accounted for. The model therefore learns how the sensors normally move
*together* at each operating point, and a fault shows up as a broken partnership that no
single threshold could see. That same pattern also suggests *where* the fault is: cooling,
air/fuel mixture, or a sensor that has stopped making sense.

## The mechanisms

Our first choice is **mechanism D, custom append-only storage with crash consistency**,
because the power disappears every time the key turns off. The device shuts itself down
cleanly on a few seconds of stored energy when it can, but a cold start, a dip at engine
start or a pulled cable can still cut it mid-write, so the storage layer must recover a
torn tail at any boot. We pair it with
**mechanism E, a multi-process architecture with a supervisor**, because a recorder that
dies silently has harmed its owner, who believes it is still on duty; running capture,
storage and analysis as separate processes means a crash in the analysis cannot take the
recording down with it.

## The risk

The primary risk, named honestly, is learning time: the model knows nothing until it has
seen weeks of a car's normal driving, so baseline collection has to start at M2, and
every week it slips is a week less of normal to compare against. The second risk is the
OBD2 protocol itself: each manufacturer implements it a little differently, a car may
not publish every sensor we would like, and some signals may be impossible to decode
because the manufacturer keeps their meaning proprietary. Finally, the scope is large for
one semester, so we are building an honest first draft of the idea, one car at a time,
one Bluetooth adapter and one Pi, rather than a finished product.

# Bill of materials

> **Nothing on this page is ordered until the paper design is signed** (D-024). Then
> order the dongle first: shipping time is the most common silent schedule-killer on this
> project (handout §16).

The product is one box with one USB-C port and one light, plus a Bluetooth OBD2 dongle in
the car's OBD2 port (D-019, D-024). The owner supplies the USB-C charger.

## Core: what we buy

| Qty | Part | ~Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Raspberry Pi 4 (2 GB+) | owned | Both partners already have one. |
| 2 | 32 GB A2 microSD | $20 | A2 endurance matters for a key-cycle soak. Two, because the soak eats cards. |
| 1 | OBDLink LX, Bluetooth Classic OBD2 dongle (STN chip) | ~$60, verify | The data path (D-019). Bluetooth Classic (SPP), **not BLE**. A cheap ELM327 Bluetooth clone is enough for the first PID survey but is unreliable for a 48 h run. |
| 1 | USB-C cable, short, 3 A-rated | $6 | From the owner's charger to the box. |
| — | USB-C car charger | owner's | Not supplied: the box takes whatever the owner has (D-024). It must go dead with the key off (`keyoff`). |
| 1 | USB-C power meter (inline) | $10 | Settles "does this charger go dead at key-off, what does it deliver, and does it sag at crank" in seconds. |

**Fallback, not ordered:** a USB OBD2 adapter with an STN chip (e.g. OBDLink SX, ~$30,
D-015) if Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car.

## The box: designed, not ordered (D-024)

Listed by function. A part number is added only with its datasheet linked and checked by
a human (`CLAUDE.md` §8.4). Sizes marked *estimate* come from the power worksheet
(`powerspec`), not from measurement.

| Qty | Function | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | USB-C receptacle, wired as a sink: 5.1 kΩ on CC1 and CC2 | The only power input. |
| 1 | Input protection: transient suppressor, reverse-polarity protection, fuse | |
| 1 | Input current limit and inrush limiter | |
| 1 | CC-level detector: comparators or a USB-C controller IC | Reports the source's advertisement (default, 1.5 A or 3 A) on GPIOs; the Pi has no analog inputs. |
| 2 | Supercapacitor cells, 2.7 V, about 20 F each (about 10 F in series) | *Estimate.* Needs cell balancing and a fuse; the temperature rating must cover a parked car's cabin. |
| 1 | Power-path controller | The source feeds the Pi first; the bank fills only the gap. |
| 1 | 5 V / 3 A converter that can step up | The bank's voltage falls as it discharges. |
| 1 | Source-present divider and halt-done switch | GPIOs chosen in the schematic (`schpi`). |
| 1 | Tri-color LED (red, yellow, green) + its resistors + the boot-time pull | The light (D-027). Two or three GPIOs, depending on the part; resistor values from its datasheet (`ledspec`). |
| 1 | Real-time clock module on I2C, with its own backup cell or capacitor | Keeps wall time while the box is off (D-030). The backup's temperature rating must cover the cabin (`rtcspec`). |
| 1 | Heatsink for the Pi | A Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C (`thermal`). |
| 1 | Shell: heat-resistant plastic (ABS, ASA or similar), vent slots, no metal near the antenna | `enclspec`. PLA softens near 60 °C, below a parked cabin's temperature. A food container is an acceptable prototype (handout). |

## Stretch — raw CAN (D-019)

Not ordered unless the stretch goal is taken up after mechanisms D and E are measured.

| Qty | Part | ~Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MCP2515 + TJA1050 CAN module | $8 | Check the crystal (8 vs 16 MHz) and meter MISO for 5 V before it touches the Pi. |
| 1 | OBD2 pass-through Y-splitter | $10 | Pins 6, 14, 5. |
| 1 | Logic analyzer (8ch clone) | $12 | Settles SPI timing arguments. |

One small box: a Pi 4, one USB-C sink input (5.1 kΩ on CC, so never more than 5 V) from
the owner's charger, fuse and transient protection, an input current and inrush limit, a

5 V / 3 A boost converter, an I2C real-time clock (D-030), a DS18B20 probe on a short
lead outside the shell (D-037) and one tri-color light (D-027). Two signals reach the
Pi: **source-present** (charger live) and, from the Pi, **halt-done**, after which the power stage cuts the Pi even if the source has returned,
then re-enables it (D-024). Nothing on the car is cut or spliced. Buyer: `hardware/BOM.md`;
builder: the schematic and `hardware/wiring.md`.

| State | Entered when | Supervisor does | Light |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOOTING` | power-on (~30 s, `bootbudget`) | start children, await heartbeats | steady yellow (hardware pull) |

### B.9 — A DS18B20 probe on the Pi, read by its own process ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-037` · Decided M2, 2026-10-26 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Revises:** D-029 (§B.7), which declined every Pi-side sensor; D-031 (§B.8), which had
one ring; D-034 (§C.5), whose sample record gains a namespace for it
· **Answers:** board item `pisensor`

**Decision.** The box gets one sensor of its own: a **DS18B20** digital temperature probe
on a short lead outside the shell, in cabin air.

- **Wiring.** The standard 1-Wire hookup: data on GPIO4 (header pin 7, the default of
  the kernel's `w1-gpio` overlay) with a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V, power from 3.3 V, not
  parasite power. Checked against the part's datasheet and drawn in the Pi interface
  block (`schpi`) before it is wired.
- **Its own process.** `ambientd` (`src/ambient/`) reads
  `/sys/bus/w1/devices/28-*/w1_slave` every 2 seconds. A reading whose CRC line ends in
  `NO`, or that holds the 85.0 °C power-on value, is rejected and logged. A missing
  device is `sensor_absent`, retried every 10 s, and `sensor_present` when it returns.
- **Its own ring.** A second shared-memory SPSC ring, `ambientd` to `storaged`, with the
  same type and the same refuse-when-full rule as the first (B.3). Each ring keeps one
  producer and one consumer, so D-031's reasons for one consumer still hold; `storaged`
  drains both into the same batches.
- **Its records.** An ordinary sample record (D-034) with `mode` 0x00, which no OBD2
  request uses, as the namespace for the box's own sensors, and `pid` 0x01 for this
  probe, value in °C.

**What it cooperates in.**

- **The cold-soak check** (sensor/electrical area). After the box has been off for hours
  (the clock says how long, D-030), coolant temperature, intake-air temperature and the
  probe should agree within a few degrees at key-on. When two agree and one does not,
  the one that disagrees is the suspect. No single threshold on one value can say that.
- **Ambient for the cooling area** when the car does not publish PID 0x46, using the
  key-on reading after a long soak.

**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-26, choosing the audit's option for two rubric risks:

- Handout §3.1 asks for at least two physically distinct sensors that cooperate. Through
  the dongle alone, every sensor reaches the Pi by one device, one link and one process,
  and a grader may call that one sensor. The probe is a second device on a second bus.
- Handout §3.2 words mechanism E as "sensors isolated in separate processes". With
  `obdd` and `ambientd`, that is now literally true, on top of the isolation of capture,
  storage and analysis (B.2).
- Demo day unplugs a sensor (handout §11). The probe is one a grader can pull by hand,
  without opening the hood of a running car.

**What it does not change.** B and F stay declined: 1-Wire's bit timing is done by the
kernel, so there is no interrupt of ours to compare against polling, and 0.5 samples a
second never stresses a ring. D and E remain the committed pair (D-017).

**Cost.**

- One part, a resistor and a GPIO; bought only after it is drawn (`probeorder`) and
  brought up on the bench with the evidence pasted (`probebench`).
- A second ring, a fifth daemon, and their rows in the failure table and the soak plot.
- The probe reads cabin air: equal to outside air only after a long soak, and
  sun-heated in summer. The design doc states this as a substitution.

**Alternative rejected.** An MPU-6050 (D-017's option): it would bring back B and F, but
it is more parts and a sensor the user's problem does not need. The written defense
alone ("the dongle is only transport"): it leaves the §3.1 question to the grader.

stored energy and stays dark until the next start. The Pi pairs with the dongle and reads

## Core: what we buy
| 1 | 5 V / 3 A converter that can step up | The bank's voltage falls as it discharges. |

| 1 | Tri-color LED (red, yellow, green) + its resistors + the boot-time pull | The light (D-027). Two or three GPIOs, depending on the part; resistor values from its datasheet (`ledspec`). |

+| 1 | DS18B20 temperature probe, waterproof, on a lead of about 1 m, + a 4.7 kΩ resistor | The box's own sensor (D-037), about $3 to $8. Bought after it is drawn (`probeorder`); powered from 3.3 V. |
| 1 | Real-time clock module on I2C, with its own backup cell or capacitor | Keeps wall time while the box is off (D-030). The backup's temperature rating must cover the cabin (`rtcspec`). |
| 1 | Heatsink for the Pi | A Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C (`thermal`). |

| 1 | Shell: heat-resistant plastic (ABS, ASA or similar), vent slots, no metal near the antenna | `enclspec`. PLA softens near 60 °C, below a parked cabin's temperature. A food container is an acceptable prototype (handout). |

content.content:
# Evaluation report — carwatch

> **STATUS: M5 SKELETON.** 3–4 pages. "Adjectives are not measurements."
> Claude can generate plausible code; it cannot fake your understanding of your own
> measurements — which is why the defense draws so heavily on this document. Every
> number in here must be one you can reproduce while someone watches.

## 1. Method and setup

Hardware, kernel version, build flags, what was running, how load was generated,
how many trials. Enough for a TA to re-measure.

**Every figure states whether its data is live, replay, or synth.** No exceptions.

## 2. Latency / timing
>
> Distributions, not just means. Under both idle and loaded CPU.

- OBD reply arrival (tty read) → durable in the log: p50 / p95 / p99 / max, idle and loaded
- Histogram, not a table of means. [figure]

## 3. Resource footprint
>
> CPU and RSS per process, at steady state and **over the full soak**. The hourly
> heartbeats give you this series for free — plot it.

[figure: RSS vs. time, all processes, every session of the 48 h key-cycle window (D-023)]

A flat line here is the whole point. A device that leaks for 48 hours and happens not
to die has not passed the soak; it has outrun it.

## 4. Domain metric
>
> The one the product lives or dies by.

Detection against the ground truth we constructed (D-021): for each induced fault, was it
flagged, how fast, and was the fault area named right, as a confusion matrix over fault
areas, with the false-positive rate called out
separately because a monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged.

## 5. Fault-injection results
>
> For each failure mode in the design document's table: what we injected, what the
> system did, and **the log excerpt proving it**.

| Injected | Expected | Observed | Light (D-027) | Log excerpt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sensor unplugged 10 min | | | | |
| `kill -9 obdd` | | | | |
| `kill -9 supervisor` | | | | |
| Power cut mid-write | | | | |
| Disk full | | | | |

## 6. Mechanism comparisons
>
> Required by our menu choices. Present as experiments: method, data, conclusion.

### 6.1 Crash consistency (mechanism D)

N power-cut trials, each cutting the Pi's 5 V rail after the converter so the supercapacitor
cannot cover it: recovery outcome each time, bytes lost per trial.

### 6.2 Supervision (mechanism E)

`kill -9` each child N times: time to detection, time to recovery, what degraded in the
meantime, and proof that no file descriptor leaked across the restart.

Mechanisms B and F were declined (D-029), so they have no comparison here.

## 7. Limitations

> Plainly. Closes the loop on the constraints and substitutions declared in
> docs/DESIGN.md §5.

"An honest limitations section is worth more at the defense than a suspiciously perfect
results section, and we notice which one we are reading."

Name at minimum: the fault areas we could not induce, what one vehicle cannot tell us
about another, how many weeks of normal the baseline actually covers, and every place a
number came from replay rather than live driving.
| Recording from key-on | A ~30 s Pi 4 boot (`bootbudget`) | The first half-minute of warm-up is lost |
| The product on the first drives | A Python tool, labeled `live` (D-033) | Proves nothing about `obdd`; enters the product only as `replay` |

## 8. Evaluation plan

> 🟨 **TEAM:** these targets are D-036, a draft; agree each number or change it.

| Measurement | Method | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |

content.content:
## 5. Storage and data

- **Format (D-034):** 40-byte header (`magic`, `kind`, `seq`, `mono_ns`, `wall_ns`, `src`,
  flags, `boot_id`), typed body, CRC32. Kinds: sample, begin, commit, boot, shutdown,
  event; a 56-byte sample keeps raw reply bytes beside the value. 16 MB segments, deleted
  whole, never edited; how long raw data is kept is open (`retention`).
- **Rates:** 10–25 samples/s is 0.56–1.4 KB/s, 2–5 MB per running hour.
- **fsync (D-035):** commit at 1 s or 64 samples, and at clean shutdown. An unclean cut
  loses at most a second (one reading per PID) of signals that move over minutes; longer
cut (`expcrash`).

**Cost.** One second of data is lost on every unclean cut, by design, and the report says
how many records each recovery dropped (D-025).

---

"""### B.10 — Events reach storage over one Unix socket to `storaged` (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-042` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Answers (if signed):** D-031's open item (§B.8) and board item `verdictpath`

**Decision (draft).** Samples travel by the rings; everything else that must be durable
is an **event**, and events travel by one socket.

- **The socket.** `storaged` listens on a Unix domain socket of type `SOCK_SEQPACKET`,
  `/run/carwatch/events.sock`, created by the supervisor's runtime directory, mode 0600.
  One packet is one event: `code` u16, then up to 200 bytes of `key=value` text. A
  sequenced packet socket keeps message boundaries and order and never splits an event.
- **Who sends.** Every daemon sends its own events: `analyzed` its verdicts (and also
  tells the supervisor, which drives the light), the supervisor its child, power and
  clock events, `obdd` and `ambientd` their link and sensor events. The event names are
  the failure table's log events (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4).
- **What `storaged` does.** It writes each event as an `event` record (D-034) in the next
  batch, so an event is durable at the same commit as the samples around it and is
  ordered with them by `seq`.
- **When `storaged` is down.** A sender keeps up to 64 unsent events in memory and drops
  the oldest beyond that, counting the drops; the count is in its heartbeat. Every event
  is also a log line in the journal at the moment it happens, so the journal is the
  record of last resort and the socket never blocks a sender (`MSG_DONTWAIT`).

**Event codes.** High byte by sender, low byte by event: `0x01` supervisor, `0x02`
`obdd`, `0x03` `ambientd`, `0x04` `analyzed` (verdicts), `0x05` `storaged` itself (for
example `recovered`, `segment_dropped`). The table of codes lives in one header,
`include/common/events.h`, and nowhere else.

**Why.** D-031 left this open, and the report (D-028) and `obdctl verdicts --since` need
verdicts and faults on disk, in order with the samples. One socket keeps `storaged` the
only writer of the log (C.1). A packet socket is the simplest IPC that keeps one event
one message. A sender that blocked on a dead `storaged` would let a storage fault stop
capture or analysis, which B.2 exists to prevent.

**Cost.** One more listener in `storaged` and one more fd per sender. Events that arrive
while `storaged` is down and overflow the 64-event queue are lost from the log (but not
from the journal), and the drop count says how many. The socket is `AF_UNIX`, so the
boundary rule must allow it outside `src/interface/` (`make boundary`).

**Alternative rejected.** Each process writing its own event file: several writers, no
common order with the samples, and one more crash-recovery story per file. Events in the
rings: the slot type is sized for a reply, and the supervisor, which has no ring, could
not send.

`D-043` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session

**Decision (draft).**

- **The control socket.** The supervisor listens on `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`, a Unix
  domain `SOCK_STREAM` socket, mode 0660. A request is one line, `VERB key=value ...`,
  at most 512 bytes. A reply is zero or more lines of `key=value` fields, then `ok`, or
  `err <code> <reason>`, then the connection closes. Text, so it can be typed by hand
  and quoted in the report and at the defense.
- **Routing.** The supervisor answers `status` itself, from its children's heartbeats.
  It forwards `verdicts`, `series` and `faults` to `storaged`, which reads its own
  committed log up to the durable offset (D-031), and `baseline` to `analyzed`, the only
  holder of baselines, each over that process's own query socket in the same format. A
  child that is down gives `err unavailable <name>`; nothing else waits on it.
- **The five verbs.**

| Verb | Arguments | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | none | each process: up, down or restarting, pid, uptime, restarts, RSS, CPU, event and drop counts; each ring's depth and overruns; dongle link and probe present or absent; the light's state; whether wall time is trusted; the mix of `src` in this session |
| `verdicts` | `--since WHEN` (default: this boot) | each surfaced verdict: start, end or active, fault area, the sensors that cooperated, residual, `src` |
| `series` | `PID --from WHEN --to WHEN [--binned]` | the samples of one PID (`0C`, or `probe`) in the window, each with `src`; `--binned` gives per-bin means instead |
| `baseline` | `PID [--bin RPM,LOAD,COOLANT]` | the learned mean and variance of one PID in every bin, or in the one bin named |
| `faults` | `--since WHEN` (default: this boot) | detection, degradation and recovery events (D-042), each with `src` |

  `WHEN` is ISO 8601 or relative (`-2h`). `obdctl` exits 0 on `ok`, 1 on `err`, 2 on a
  usage error and 3 when the supervisor cannot be reached.

  process, `statusd`, in `src/interface/`. It serves HTTP only on the box's access-point
  address, and builds every page and report from the same control-socket verbs, so it
  holds no state of its own. It is the only process with an `AF_INET` socket.

supervisor without saying how, the README's `baseline` line was ambiguous about bins,

the page and a human at a terminal ask the same questions. History is answered by

never slow the restart path.

content.content:
1	# Design document — carwatch
2	
3	> **WEDNESDAY REVIEW — delete this box, and every 🟨 / 📏 note, before submitting.**
4	> 🟨 **TEAM** = decide or review together. 📏 **DRIVE** = replace with a number from the
5	> first Forester drive (`firstcap`, `pidforester`). Checklist:
6	>
7	> - [ ] Sign, change or reject D-019 to D-036 in `DECISIONS.md` (the doc cites them).
8	> - [ ] Decide the fault-area rows in §3 and fill the ownership map in §9.
9	> - [ ] Drive numbers into §1, §3 and §5; Lance's power numbers into §6.
10	> - [ ] Three-isolated-workers check: design-only reader, BOM-only buyer, wiring-only
11	>   builder each succeed from their own part.
12	> - [ ] Render to PDF: 5 pages or fewer without this box.
13	
14	**User and problem.** Lance drives a 2015 CR-V daily, and nothing reads his engine's
15	sensors except a check-engine light that speaks only once something has failed. carwatch
16	is a box that boots at every key-on, records every Mode 01 sensor through a Bluetooth
17	OBD2 dongle, learns *this* car's normal, and flags behavior that leaves it before the
18	light would. It is also tested on Camden's 2008 Forester (D-022). **Claim (D-021):** it
19	learns the normal of the car it is installed in, flags behavior outside it and names the
20	likely fault area, with measured catch and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.
21	
22	## 1. Architecture
23	
24	```text
25	OBD2 port -- OBDLink LX (Bluetooth SPP, D-019)   DS18B20 cabin probe (D-037)
26	   ~~ RFCOMM ~~> BlueZ -> rfcomm tty -> /dev/obd    1-Wire -> kernel w1-gpio -> sysfs
27	  obdd    Mode 01, one outstanding, ~10-25 req/s   ambientd   one read every 2 s
28	    | ring 1: SPSC, ~10-25 samples/s                  | ring 2: SPSC, 0.5 samples/s
29	    +------------------------+------------------------+  shared memory, refuse when full
30	                             v
31	  storaged [D]  BEGIN..COMMIT batches, 1 fsync/s, ~1 KB/s -> ext4 on SD (D-025)
32	    ^           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few a drive (D-042)
33	    | committed records only, read back from the log, ~1 s behind (D-031)
34	    v
35	  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> model -> FSM
36	    | verdicts over a Unix socket, a few per drive at most
37	    v
38	  supervisor [E] spawns, heartbeats, restarts with backoff --GPIO--> light,

54	## 2. Mechanism mapping
55	
56	D and E are the committed pair (D-017); B and F stay declined: Mode 01 and a 0.5 Hz
57	probe never stress a ring, and the probe's 1-Wire timing belongs to the kernel, not to
58	us (D-029, D-037).

60	| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
61	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
62	| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power can vanish at any instant (empty bank at a cold start, pulled cable, crank reset, D-024), yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn from a sample a cut later erased (D-031). 63	| E | `supervisor`, `src/ipc/` | A recorder that dies silently harms an owner who thinks it is on duty; the least trusted code (analysis) must not take capture or storage down (B.2). Each sensor source has its own process: a hung Bluetooth link cannot stop the probe, nor a dead probe the engine sensors (D-037) | `kill -9` each child 20×: detection, recovery, fd leaks |
64	
65	**Two physically distinct sensors that cooperate (handout §3.1).** The DS18B20 probe on
66	the Pi and the car's coolant and intake-air sensors are different devices on different
67	buses, read by different processes (D-037). They cooperate in the cold-soak check (§3):
68	after hours off (the clock says how long, D-030) all three should agree, and the one
69	that disagrees is the suspect. Beyond the probe, the engine's sensors are distinct
70	transducers the dongle only carries, and every diagnostic fuses at least two (D.4). "Both
71	sensors alive" (M2) means a real Mode 01 capture and a pasted probe reading; "through the
72	pipeline" (M3) means both arrive as committed records labeled `live`.

74	## 3. Analysis: how normal is learned and a fault area named
75	
76	All our code (handout §3.3; D.1, D.2). Per committed sample, `analyzed` (1) bins by
77	rpm × load × coolant temperature, so a cold idle is never compared with a warm cruise;
78	(2) keeps per-bin running mean and covariance (Welford), in A/B checkpoints; (3) scores the
79	Mahalanobis distance from the bin's baseline, which fires when a *partnership* breaks;
80	(4) fits Theil–Sen slopes of residuals across drives; (5) names the area with our
81	classifier (trained in `tools/train/`, inference in C; without weights, 1–4 still flag);
82	(6) surfaces verdicts through a hysteresis-and-dwell state machine (D.3).

84	| Fault area (D-021) | Cooperating sensors | Signature | Induced by (E.2) |
85	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
86	| Cooling | coolant, intake temp, ambient (PID 0x46, else the probe), load, speed | warm-up slope or warm settling temperature off its bin's normal for the same ambient and load | cardboard over the radiator |

88	| Sensor/electrical | the failed PID and its usual partners; module voltage; at a cold start, coolant, intake temp and the probe | one PID absent or flat while its partners move; after a long soak, one temperature off the other two | a sensor unplugged |
89	| Unknown | all | residual high, no area matches | — |

92	move together, inside one bin (D.4). 📏 **DRIVE:** strike any sensor the survey shows the
93	Forester does not publish.

96	> Claude's proposal from D-021 and D.2. The AI-use plan (§10) says analysis design is
97	> ours, so confirm, change or replace each row, and then delete this note.

99	## 4. Failure-mode table
100	
101	Log lines are `<process> <level> <event> key=value` with `src`; the table names the event.
102	
103	| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log event |
104	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
105	| adapter | Bluetooth drops | `read` 0/`EIO`, `POLLHUP` | reopen `/dev/obd` with backoff | `link_lost`, `reconnected` |
106	| adapter | garbage or timeouts | parse failure; timeout | 3 in a row: `ATZ`, then reopen | `reply_bad`, `adapter_reset` |
107	| adapter | engine off, key in ACC | `0100` gets `NO DATA` | poll `0100` every few s, record nothing | `ecu_silent` |
108	| ECU | a sensor unplugged or failed | 5 `NO DATA` in a row; or the value pinned or flat while its partners move, with the MIL on and the DTC count up (PID 0101) | mark absent or suspect, retry each minute; report it. Most ECUs substitute a default value and light the CEL, so this fault is not caught before the light | `pid_absent`, `pid_flat`, `mil_on`, `pid_present` |
109	| probe | unplugged, broken wire, bad read | device gone from sysfs; CRC `NO`; the 85.0 °C power-on value | mark absent, retry every 10 s; cold-soak check off, reported | `sensor_absent`, `sensor_present`, `reply_bad` |
110	| any child | crash, `kill -9` | `waitpid` | restart with backoff; others run on | `child_exit`, `child_restart` |
111	| ring | consumer stalls | sequence gap; late heartbeat | refuse and count (B.3); restart `storaged`; red | `ring_full`, `heartbeat_late` |
112	| storaged | power cut mid-write | bad CRC / no `COMMIT` at boot | truncate tail and open batch (D-025) | `recovered` |
113	| storaged | disk full; `fsync` or write `EIO` | `ENOSPC`, return values | drop oldest segment if allowed; hold durable offset; degrade, red | `enospc`, `fsync_failed` |
114	| analyzed | torn checkpoint; bad model file | slot CRC; header CRC | other slot + redo; residuals only | `checkpoint_bad`, `model_unavailable` |
115	| `statusd` | report fails, out of memory | error; RSS | page says so; capture unaffected | `report_failed` |
116	| supervisor | dies | systemd `Restart=always` | light freezes steady = "not running" | journal |
117	| clock | RTC lost backup (D-030) | invalid time at boot | run on `mono_ns`; wall time untrusted | `rtc_invalid` |
118	| power | key-off, cable pulled, crank dip, source back mid-shutdown | source-present GPIO timing | §6 state machine | `source_lost`, `source_dip`, `shutdown` |

120	| power, heat | undervoltage, throttling, charger live at key-off | `vcgencmd`, SoC temp | degrade, log, report; halt policy open | `undervoltage`, `thermal` |

123	## 5. Storage and data
124	
125	- **Format (D-034):** 40-byte header (`magic`, `kind`, `seq`, `mono_ns`, `wall_ns`, `src`,
126	  flags, `boot_id`), typed body, CRC32. Kinds: sample, begin, commit, boot, shutdown,
127	  event; a 56-byte sample keeps raw reply bytes beside the value. 16 MB segments, never
128	  edited.

131	  then whole segments go oldest first, never one the newest checkpoint still needs. A
132	  32 GB card holds years of two-hour days. Text logs go to the journal, size-capped.
133	- **fsync (D-035):** commit at 1 s or 64 samples, and at clean shutdown. An unclean cut
134	  loses at most a second (one reading per PID) of signals that move over minutes; longer
135	  batches lose warm-up at each cold-start reset; per-record `fsync` is 20× the flash wear.

137	  truncates the torn tail and any uncommitted batch (undo is truncation: nothing is
138	  overwritten), and logs whether the last session ended clean. `analyzed` loads the newest
139	  valid checkpoint and redoes later batches through the live code path (D-025).
