141	## 6. The box: hardware and safe power-down
142	
143	One small box: a Pi 4, one USB-C sink input (5.1 kΩ on CC, so never more than 5 V) from
144	the owner's charger, fuse and transient protection, an input current and inrush limit, a
145	supercapacitor bank (two 2.7 V cells, about 10 F, about 105 J usable, estimate) behind a
146	5 V / 3 A boost converter, an I2C real-time clock (D-030), a DS18B20 probe on a short
147	lead outside the shell (D-037) and one tri-color light (D-027). Two signals reach the
148	Pi: **source-present** (charger live) and, from the Pi, **halt-done**, after which the
149	power stage cuts the Pi even if the source has returned, then re-enables it (D-024).
150	Nothing on the car is cut or spliced. Buyer: `hardware/BOM.md`; builder: the schematic
151	and `hardware/wiring.md`.

154	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
155	| `BOOTING` | power-on (~30 s, `bootbudget`) | start children, await heartbeats | steady yellow (hardware pull) |
156	| `RUNNING` | all healthy, source present | record | green pulse |
157	| `DEGRADED` | child down, dongle silent with engine on, storage or power fault | record what it can; log absent vs crashed | red blink |
158	| `GRACE` | source-present lost | keep recording; source back → `RUNNING` (a crank dip) | yellow blink |
159	| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | grace (~3 s) expires | stop `obdd`, final `COMMIT` + `fsync`, checkpoint, `sync`, halt; source back → finish, then reboot | yellow blink |
160	| `OFF` | halt-done; power stage cuts the Pi | nothing | dark |
161

168	> a charger stays live with the engine silent (`shutfsm`).

179	| Full hold-up | Owner's charger + seconds-scale supercapacitor (D-024) | A cold-start crank may reset the Pi |

181	| The product on the first drives | A Python tool, labeled `live` (D-033) | Proves nothing about `obdd`; enters the product only as `replay` |

185	> 🟨 **TEAM:** these targets are D-036, a draft; agree each number or change it.

188	| --- | --- | --- |
189	| Reply → durable, p50 / p99 | timestamps at tty read and after `fsync`; idle and with a CPU hog | ≤ 1.2 s / ≤ 2.5 s |
190	| Sustained request rate | answers per second from the log, per drive | ≥ 10/s; every model input every ≤ 2 s |
191	| `kill -9` each child | 20 trials per child, from the log | detect ≤ 100 ms; heartbeat ≤ 5 s; no fd leak |
192	| Ring drops under contention (B.3) | sequence accounting, both rings | 0 |
193	| CPU per process | `utime` + `stime` from `/proc/<pid>/stat` in every heartbeat; idle and with a CPU hog | each daemon ≤ 10 % of one core; all ≤ 25 % |
194	| RSS over the soak | heartbeats at start, hourly, end, per session | slope < 100 KB per running hour |
195	| fsync batch size (`expbatch`) | per record, 1 s and 10 s batches on the Pi's SD: `fsync` p50 / p99, bytes written, records lost per cut | 1 s loses ≤ 1 s per cut and writes ≤ ⅕ of per-record's bytes |

213	| `src/obd/`, `src/ambient/`, the `storaged` write and recovery path, `src/analysis/`, `src/supervisor/`, `src/interface/`, `tools/train/`, `electricalDrawing/` | unclaimed | scaffolds only so far |

219	
220	Claude Code is used for planning, explaining kernel and serial mechanics, test fixtures,
221	tooling, adversarial review of diffs and documentation, and drafting; never at runtime.
222	It may draft any part of the design, the analysis included, but a draft binds nothing:

  overwritten), and logs whether the last session ended clean. `analyzed` loads the newest
  valid checkpoint and redoes later batches through the live code path (D-025).

## 6. The box: hardware and safe power-down

One small box: a Pi 4, one USB-C sink input (5.1 kΩ on CC, so never more than 5 V) from
the owner's charger, fuse and transient protection, an input current and inrush limit, a
supercapacitor bank (two 2.7 V cells, about 10 F, about 105 J usable, estimate) behind a
5 V / 3 A boost converter, an I2C real-time clock (D-030), a DS18B20 probe on a short
lead outside the shell (D-037) and one tri-color light (D-027). Two signals reach the
Pi: **source-present** (charger live) and, from the Pi, **halt-done**, after which the
power stage cuts the Pi even if the source has returned, then re-enables it (D-024).
Nothing on the car is cut or spliced. Buyer: `hardware/BOM.md`; builder: the schematic
and `hardware/wiring.md`.

| State | Entered when | Supervisor does | Light |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOOTING` | power-on (~30 s, `bootbudget`) | start children, await heartbeats | steady yellow (hardware pull) |
| `RUNNING` | all healthy, source present | record | green pulse |
| `DEGRADED` | child down, dongle silent with engine on, storage or power fault | record what it can; log absent vs crashed | red blink |
| `GRACE` | source-present lost | keep recording; source back → `RUNNING` (a crank dip) | yellow blink |
| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | grace (~3 s) expires | stop `obdd`, final `COMMIT` + `fsync`, checkpoint, `sync`, halt; source back → finish, then reboot | yellow blink |
| `OFF` | halt-done; power stage cuts the Pi | nothing | dark |

Energy (estimates, D-024): grace plus shutdown need 65–85 J of about 105 J usable. A
crash at any point is still recovered by mechanism D.

> 🟨 **TEAM / LANCE (Wednesday):** the power block's parts, the bank size, the grace
> period and the shutdown time are estimates until `powerspec` and `capbench` measure
> them; replace each with a number or mark it "estimate". Decide what the box does when
> a charger stays live with the engine silent (`shutfsm`).

## 7. Constraints and substitutions

| Wanted | Using | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every engine sensor | The Mode 01 PIDs the ECU publishes (D-022) | Oil pressure likely absent; lists differ by car |
| Outside air temperature | A DS18B20 in the cabin (D-037) | Reads cabin air: ambient only after a long soak, and sun-heated in summer |
| Failing engines | Induced, reversible faults on two healthy cars (D-021) | A few fault areas; no real wear-out |
| Raw CAN at ECU rate | Bluetooth Mode 01 request/response (D-019) | ~10–25 samples/s, no bus timing, a link that drops; most of the menu leaves the data path (D-017) |
| 48 continuous hours | 48 h of normal use across key cycles (D-023) | Sessions with gaps; the professor confirmed this reading (D-023) |
| Full hold-up | Owner's charger + seconds-scale supercapacitor (D-024) | A cold-start crank may reset the Pi |
| Recording from key-on | A ~30 s Pi 4 boot (`bootbudget`) | The first half-minute of warm-up is lost |
| The product on the first drives | A Python tool, labeled `live` (D-033) | Proves nothing about `obdd`; enters the product only as `replay` |

## 8. Evaluation plan

| Measurement | Method | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reply → durable, p50 / p99 | timestamps at tty read and after `fsync`; idle and with a CPU hog | ≤ 1.2 s / ≤ 2.5 s |
| Sustained request rate | answers per second from the log, per drive | ≥ 10/s; every model input every ≤ 2 s |
| `kill -9` each child | 20 trials per child, from the log | detect ≤ 100 ms; heartbeat ≤ 5 s; no fd leak |
| Ring drops under contention (B.3) | sequence accounting, both rings | 0 |
| CPU per process | `utime` + `stime` from `/proc/<pid>/stat` in every heartbeat; idle and with a CPU hog | each daemon ≤ 10 % of one core; all ≤ 25 % |
| RSS over the soak | heartbeats at start, hourly, end, per session | slope < 100 KB per running hour |
| fsync batch size (`expbatch`) | per record, 1 s and 10 s batches on the Pi's SD: `fsync` p50 / p99, bytes written, records lost per cut | 1 s loses ≤ 1 s per cut and writes ≤ ⅕ of per-record's bytes |
| Every failure-table row (§4) | inject it as EVALUATION.md §5 lists; read the log | its log event appears; a fault outside capture never stops capture |
| Probe unplugged (D-037) | pull it with everything running | `sensor_absent` ≤ 10 s; engine capture unaffected |

# Supported-PID survey

**Sets the model's input list (D-007, D-021). Run this before M2.**

Method: with the OBD2 adapter (D-019) paired and bound as `/dev/obd`, open it in a
terminal (`screen /dev/obd`; the baud is ignored over Bluetooth) and send `ATZ`, `ATE0`,
`ATSP0`, then `0100`, `0120`, `0140`, `0160`. Each reply is a 32-bit
bitmap of which PIDs in the next block the ECU supports. Ten minutes; paste the raw
replies below the table, dated.

## What we specifically need to know

Vehicles (D-022): Camden's **2008 Subaru Forester** (non-turbo; OBD protocol not yet
verified, expected CAN) and Lance's **2015 Honda CR-V EX-L** (D-007; engine and
transmission still to be confirmed from the VIN). For each car, also record the protocol
the adapter negotiated (`ATDP`) and the VIN (Mode 09, `0902`).

| PID | Signal | Forester | CR-V | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x0C | RPM | | | |
| 0x04 | Calculated load | | | |
| 0x05 | Coolant temp | | | |
| 0x0F | Intake air temp | | | |
| 0x0B | MAP | | | |
| 0x06/0x07 | Short/long term fuel trim B1 | | | |
| 0x5C | Engine oil temp | | | |
| — | Oil pressure | | | Usually not a standard PID; the CR-V likely has only a switch. Nothing depends on it (D-021). |
| 0x2F | Fuel level | | | |
| 0x31 | Distance since codes cleared | | | odometer proxy |

## After the survey

Every supported PID in the table above becomes an input to the model for that car. Record
which ones each car answers, with the raw replies, and update the sensor list in
`docs/DESIGN.md` §4.
Manufacturer (Mode 22) PIDs are a stretch: try them only if a fault area has too few
sensors to call.

# Decision log — carwatch

**Purpose:** every design decision on this project, in one place, organized by category so
you can find what you need without knowing an ID. This is an **audit log**, not a
reference doc — its job is to let Camden and Lance verify, after any working session,
that no decision was made on their behalf that they disagree with.

**This file holds what is DECIDED. Open work and open questions live on the GitHub
board** as issues with milestones, and no pre-assigned owners (D-026, `CLAUDE.md` §7.11).
An ❓ OPEN entry below exists only as a pointer to its issue, so the reasoning sits beside
the decisions it will eventually join.

| D-043 | Draft control socket: a line protocol on `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`, the five `obdctl` verbs with their arguments, and `statusd` as the page process (§B.11) | Claude, Camden's session | 2026-10-27 | Both — it is the whole query interface, and the live-modification station will extend it |
| D-041 | Draft retention: every segment kept until the disk is 80 % full, then oldest whole segments first, never one a checkpoint needs (§C.7) | Claude, Camden's session | 2026-10-27 | Both — it is how long the device remembers |
| D-036 | Draft evaluation targets: latency, kill-and-recover, drops, memory, detection and crash recovery, each with a number (§E.4) | Claude, Camden's session | 2026-10-26 | Both — numbers committed at M2 are what M5 is judged against |
| D-032 | Python tools are tested with stdlib `unittest` in a venv that `make test` builds on first use (§F.6) | Camden (in session) + Claude | 2026-10-26 | Either — it adds a step to `make test` and installs two pinned packages |
| D-026 | No pre-assigned owners; a subsystem belongs to its first substantive commit; supersedes 🔒 F.2 (§F.2) | Camden (reopened F.2) + Claude | 2026-10-21 | Lance — it removes every assignment the M0 map gave you, and changes CLAUDE.md §0 and §6 |

> Decisions marked 🔒 were made with Camden in the conversation. **Lance has not reviewed
> any of them yet** — Lance, read at minimum §B.1, §C.1 and §D.1, since those bind storage
> and analysis.
89:BLE) plugs into the OBD2 port. The Pi, powered from the car's USB (D-011), talks to it with
944:**Provisional numbers (estimates).** One `COMMIT` and one `fsync` per batch of about one

**Reviewer note.** This is a real trade: under sustained overload we drop *new* data
rather than *old*. If that is ever the wrong choice for a diagnostic, reopen this.
+### B.4 — The phone is a read-only window over the device's own Wi-Fi ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
+`D-013` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
+· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
+*Extended 2026-10-21 by D-028 (§B.6): the page also shows trends and downloads a report,
+and the server-language sub-decision below is closed (C).*
+**Decision.** The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi access point — WPA2, a per-device passphrase, **no
+upstream connection, no internet**. The owner's phone joins it and opens a status page
+served from `src/interface/` by a supervised child process. The page shows exactly two
+things — **status** and **current verdicts** — rendered from the same supervisor UDS verbs
+`obdctl` uses. It holds no state, runs no analysis, and writes nothing. `obdctl` remains
+the primary, exact interface with all five verbs. No app, no account, no cloud, and the
+phone never pairs over Bluetooth. (The Pi itself pairs with the OBD2 adapter, D-019.)
+**Why.** The user is a car owner, not someone with a terminal in the passenger seat, so a
+product that can only be read over SSH has no user. The handout permits it directly
+("Serving a dashboard on the LAN is fine", §3.3; CLAUDE.md §2.1), and the device keeps
+working with no phone present at all. It also sharpens the phone-app test: the Pi is the
+part that is awake at every key-on; the phone is only a window onto what it already
+recorded.
+**Why so thin.** The handout warns: *"Resist the pretty web app. A crisp CLI with five
+query verbs and exact semantics is more defensible, and far more extensible at the
+live-modification station."* So the page is a view, not a second interface: two screens,
+no framework, and no number on it that `obdctl` cannot also produce. Every graded behavior
+remains demonstrable through `obdctl` alone.
+**Cost.**
+- A network listener in the product. It binds only to the AP interface, is read-only, and
+  lives only in `src/interface/`, where `make boundary` already allows network symbols.
+- One more process in the 48-hour RSS plot, and Wi-Fi radio power from the box's supply
+- The access point shares the Pi 4's one radio chip with the Bluetooth link to the adapter
+  (D-019). Measured by `btcoex`.
+- **Sub-decision, closed by D-028:** the server's language. C in `src/interface/` keeps an
+  interpreter out of the memory-stability test; Python in `ui/` is permitted by CLAUDE.md
+  §2.5 but adds ~30 MB RSS to the soak. Recommendation: C, because the page is tiny.
+  Camden chose C, 2026-10-21.
+### B.5 — One tri-color status light, and every live state pulses ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
+`D-027` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
+· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
+· **Supersedes:** D-014 (§G.10)
+**Decision.** One LED, visible through the shell, shows red, yellow or green. It is
+written **only by the supervisor** (D-014's rule, kept).
+| Light | Meaning |
+| green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go |
+| yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: riding a supply dip, or shutting down |
+| red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** in the car; the report says which |
+| steady yellow | Booting: held on from power-up, before the supervisor runs |
+| any other steady light, or dark while the car runs | **Not running.** Never a valid live state |
+| dark while the car is off | Normal: the box is off |
+Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green. Steady yellow for more
+than about a minute means the boot never finished.
+**What counts as red.** In the box: a child down or restart-limited; the dongle silent
+while the engine runs; storage failing or nearly full; undervoltage or thermal
+throttling; the supercapacitor's self-check failed. In the car: a verdict has surfaced
+after hysteresis and dwell (D.3), or a sensor the car stopped answering.
+**Why every live state pulses.** D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors: a GPIO keeps
+its last level after the process driving it dies, so a steady green would freeze into a
+false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If every live state blinks, a frozen light of
+any color can only mean "not running". Camden asked for whichever pattern is safer (P11),
+and this is.
+**The boot state.** The Pi spends roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`) booting
+before any software can drive the light. Yellow is held on from power-up in hardware: a
+pull keeps it lit while its GPIO is still an input, and once the supervisor drives the
+pin, the pin wins. Camden's choice (R4). The firmware's `gpio=` setting in `config.txt`
+might do the same with no parts; confirm on the board before relying on it.
+**Open (`ledspec`).** What the light shows after the supervisor takes the GPIOs but before
+every child's first heartbeat. Yellow blink is taken (stored energy). Claude's
+recommendation, not decided: the supervisor keeps yellow steady until its first
+all-healthy check, so the light still reads "not running yet".
+**The part.** Whether yellow is its own die or red and green mixed is a part choice (two
+GPIOs or three), made in `ledspec` from the LED's datasheet, which also sets the
+resistors. Pins are assigned in the schematic (`schpi`).
+**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P10, P11): one light, three
+colors, and red means an issue in either the box or the car.
+**Cost.** Two or three GPIOs instead of one; the supervisor's blink timer still must never
+delay `waitpid` handling; the colors must stay distinguishable through the shell
+(`enclspec`). Red merges box and car issues, so the report must say which.
+**Alternative rejected.** D-014's single-color patterns (a double-blink for a verdict): a
+pattern code the owner has to learn.
+### B.6 — The phone page also downloads a report; an app is a stretch ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
+`D-028` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
+· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
+**Decision.** The status page (D-013) shows status, current verdicts and trends, and has
+one button: **Download report**. The report is one self-contained HTML file plus a CSV of
+the same data, generated on the box by a C program in `src/interface/`. The page still
+writes nothing to the device. A native phone app is a stretch goal, not planned for M2 to
+**Report contents** (first draft; finalized in `reportspec`):
+| Section | Content |
+| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy, and the mix of data sources (`live`, `replay`, `synth`), always labeled (C.2) |
+| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
+| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, the supercapacitor's self-check, free storage |
+| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, the sensors that cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
+| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
+| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |
+**Reachability.** The box is off whenever the car is (D-024), so a phone reaches it only
+while the car runs, or while the box is plugged into any USB-C charger at home, where it
+boots and serves the same page.
+**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P12): the owner views data and
+trends on a phone and downloads a report that says what is wrong with the box or the car.
+HTML opens on any phone with no app, and the CSV lets the owner or a mechanic take the
+numbers elsewhere. C, as D-013 recommended: the server is small, and an interpreter would
+add tens of megabytes to the 48-hour memory plot (R3).
+**Rule kept from D-013.** The report is assembled from the same supervisor UDS verbs
+`obdctl` uses, so every number in it can also be produced at the CLI, and every graded
+behavior stays demonstrable through `obdctl` alone.
+**Cost.** A report generator is new code in the product: it gets rows in the failure
+table, its memory shows in the soak plot, and the boundary check still has to show the
+page is the only network code.
+**Alternatives rejected.** A PDF report (needs a PDF writer we would have to defend). A
+native app (a second product to build). A Python server in `ui/` (the soak's memory).

1	# carwatch — full project plan
     2	
     3	**This file is the *why*. `docs/milestones.md` is the *what*.**
     4	
     5	The work breakdown that used to live here — 80 numbered tasks with owners and blocked-by
     6	lists — is now the checklist in `docs/milestones.md`, which `tools/board_sync.py` mirrors
     7	onto GitHub issues and the `carwatch` project board (D-020). Keeping a second copy here
     8	would guarantee the two disagreed by Week 9, and nothing would have told us which one was
     9	wrong.
    10	
    11	So: read **this** for why the plan is shaped this way and what to sacrifice when it slips.
    12	Read **the board** for what to do next. See `docs/BOARD/BOARD.md` for how the board works.
    13	
    14	- Decisions already made: `docs/DECISIONS.md`
    15	- Milestone exit criteria: `docs/milestones.md`
    16	- The rubric itself: `docs/handout/CS370-TermProject.md`
    17	
    18	Items are named below by their **slug**, the short name in backticks at the end of their
    19	line in `docs/milestones.md`.
    20	
    21	---
    22	
    23	## 1. The two critical paths
    24	
    25	Everything else has slack. These two do not, and they are the only reasons this project
    26	fails in Week 14.
    27	
    28	### Critical path A — calendar, not effort: learning the car's normal
    29	
    30	The model knows nothing until it has seen a car's normal driving: cold starts, short
    31	trips and long pulls, across weeks. **That is calendar time you cannot buy back by working
    32	harder** (D-021).
    33	
    34	```text
    35	baseline collection starts ──── weeks of normal driving ────▶ induced faults ────▶ measured
    36	        M2 (mid-Oct)                                               M4                  M5
    37	```
    38	
    39	**Consequence:** logging must be running on a real car by the end of M2, even if the code
    40	is ugly, even if it is just raw adapter replies logged to a file. A crude capture that starts
    41	on time beats an elegant one that starts three weeks late. Every week it slips is a week
    42	less of normal to learn from, and a weaker catch rate at M5.

1	# Revision plan: the box redesign and the road to M2
2	
3	> **STATUS: PROPOSAL, written 2026-10-21 in Camden's session. Nothing in this file is a
4	> decision.** A decision exists only when it is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` as
5	> ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, in the same commit as whatever enacts it, and signed later by a human.
6	> Claude never marks a decision reviewed or 🔒 LOCKED (`CLAUDE.md` §0).
7	>
8	> **Update, later on 2026-10-21: stage 1 is done** on branch `camden/m2/revision-plan`.
9	> D-022 to D-031 are in `docs/DECISIONS.md` as ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, with every dependent doc
10	> edit. Where this file and `DECISIONS.md` disagree, `DECISIONS.md` wins. What was
11	> answered, and what is still open, is marked in §1.2, §4.2 and §11.
12	>
13	> **Audience: a fresh Claude session with no memory of the conversation that produced this
14	> file.** Everything it needs is here or named by path. Where this file says "Camden
15	> decided", that is a statement about the 2026-10-21 conversation, and §1 says exactly
16	> which statements those are. Everything else is Claude's recommendation and must be
17	> confirmed with Camden before it is written down as settled.
18	
19	## 0. How to use this file
20	
21	1. Do the session-start steps in `CLAUDE.md` §0 first (read `docs/milestones.md`, the
22	   review queue at the top of `docs/DECISIONS.md`, run the board status, check `git
23	   status` is clean, `git pull`, create a branch **before** the first edit).
24	2. Read §1 (provenance), then §2 and §3 (the product and its engineering numbers), then
25	   §4 (what is wrong in the repo today).
26	3. Work through §8 in order. Each stage is one pull request; each commit inside it is one
27	   responsibility (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3). Do not skip ahead: later stages assume the earlier
28	   decisions exist.
29	4. Stop and ask Camden at every item in §11. Do not guess at them.
30	5. Obey §12 (the do-not list) at all times.
31	6. At the end of the session do the `CLAUDE.md` §0 end steps, including the transcript
32	   copy-out (`partners/camden/transcripts/README.md` now has the macOS command).
33	
34	This plan edits documents first and code later. No money is spent by anything in it
35	(§10). Camden's standing instruction: be very sure of the paper plan before any part is
36	bought.
37	
38	## 1. Provenance: what Camden decided, and what Claude only recommended
39	
40	### 1.1 Decided by Camden in the 2026-10-21 conversation
41	
42	| # | Statement |
43	| --- | --- |
44	| P1 | The team's 2008 Subaru Forester (non-turbo, Camden's car) is a testbed. Lance's 2015 Honda CR-V remains Lance's to use. **Neither car is required of anyone, and no document may restrict where either partner tests.** Camden's instruction, paraphrased: do not set limitations or restrictions for him, and especially not for Lance while the two of them are not communicating. |
45	| P2 | Tasks have no pre-assigned owners. Any open task is for whoever is available. For the handout's per-subsystem map, Camden chose **claim on first commit**: whoever lands a subsystem's first substantive commit is recorded as its owner. |
46	| P3 | The professor said the 48-hour soak means **48 hours of regular use** (not 48 hours powered): the car starts and stops, the product handles every cycle, is on and working every time the car runs, shuts down gracefully when the car shuts off, and auto-boots on the next start. Camden chose the reading "48 hours wall-clock of normal use". This has **not** been received in writing. |
47	| P4 | Camden approved **extending locked decision C.1** (append-only, CRC'd records) with write-ahead-log style transactions and checkpoints: a batch is `BEGIN`, records, `COMMIT`; recovery redoes committed work from the latest checkpoint and undoes uncommitted work. Camden's reason: it ties the project to the logging and checkpoint techniques taught in class. |
48	| P5 | `pisensor` (an MPU-6050 or similar on the Pi for mechanisms B and F) is **declined**. Mechanisms D and E stay the committed pair. |
49	| P6 | The Raspberry Pi 4 stays (both partners already own one). |
50	| P7 | **The product is one box.** The box has a single clean USB-C port (like a computer's) as its only power input. The user plugs in whatever USB-C charger and cable they already own. Camden: "no need to reinvent the charger." The team designs the box; the team buys only the OBD2 Bluetooth dongle and a cable. The box limits what any source can push, and supplements weak power from a small stored-energy element. |
51	| P8 | The stored-energy element is **small and short-lived by design**: its jobs are supplementing weak input power, bridging the dip at engine start, and giving the Pi enough time for a clean shutdown. It is **never** an always-on source and is not to be designed as one; about one minute of stored runtime is the ceiling and a few seconds to tens of seconds is the goal. The Pi is **intentionally off at rest**, which is what makes the 48-hour soak definition (P3) valid. |
52	| P9 | The Bluetooth OBD2 dongle is assumed to work as expected (Bluetooth Classic serial profile, **not BLE**). The box reads it, logs, and processes the data. |
53	| P10 | **Wake button: dropped.** The box has one port and one light and no buttons. |
54	| P11 | **One tri-color light.** Red means an issue, and "issue" means either a problem with the box or a problem with the car; the report says which. Yellow means starting or stopping on stored energy. Green means ready, all systems go. For pulse versus steady, Camden said whichever is safer, so §2.3 specifies pulsing. |
55	| P12 | The phone connects to the box (its own Wi-Fi) to view data and trends and to **download a report**. An app is "maybe": a stretch, not a commitment. |
56	| P13 | The box is "super small, sleek", with vents if needed. |
57	| P14 | **No shopping for now.** The paper plan comes first. |
58	
59	### 1.2 Recommended by Claude, not confirmed by Camden (confirm before recording)
60	
61	| # | Recommendation | Why it is still open |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| R1 | The stored-energy element is a **supercapacitor bank**, not a lithium cell. | Camden said "small rechargeable battery" first, then described the seconds-scale role. He never chose the chemistry. §3.1 has the reasoning (no thermal runaway, no charge-temperature cutoff to design, works in a hot or frozen car). |
64	| R2 | A **short grace period** after the source disappears, longer than a crank dip and shorter than the stored runtime, before shutdown starts. | Needs the Forester's real supply-dip measurement. |
65	| R3 | **Report as one HTML file plus a CSV**, served by a C program in `src/interface/`. | Camden said "report" and "maybe an app". Format is unchosen. |
66	| R4 | Steady yellow while booting (a not-yet-running state), pulses everywhere once alive. | See §2.3 and §11. |
67	| R5 | The phone page may set the Pi's clock (the Pi has no battery-backed clock). | Conflicts with D-013's "writes nothing". §11. |
68	| R6 | Record the Forester as the car the first baseline and fault captures run on. | Follows from P1 but is not itself a decision about Lance. |
69	
70	**Answered by Camden, 2026-10-21, and recorded:** R1 supercapacitor (D-024). R3 HTML plus
71	CSV served by C (D-028). R4 steady yellow held in hardware (D-027). R5 no: a real-time
72	clock keeps the time instead, and the page stays read-only (D-030). **Still open:** R2,
73	the grace period's length, which needs `cranklog`. R6 was not recorded: P1 says no car is
74	required, so D-022 names both cars and neither as first.
75	
76	### 1.3 Unknown, must be measured or asked
77	
78	| # | Unknown | How to resolve |
79	| --- | --- | --- |
80	| U1 | Which Mode 01 PIDs the Forester answers, and its OBD protocol. A 2008 US car is expected to speak CAN (ISO 15765-4) but this is **not verified**. MAP may be absent. | PID survey (§8, stage 3). Do not assume; the sensor list and fault areas depend on it. |
81	| U2 | The Forester's supply behavior at crank, and whether its sockets and ports switch with the key. | Meter. Free first test: a USB charger with a light in the socket, key off. |
82	| U3 | Real Pi 4 boot and shutdown time and power draw on this image. | USB-C power meter and `systemd-analyze`. |
83	| U4 | The professor's written confirmation of the soak definition (P3). | Email, drafted in §9. Camden sends it. |
84	| U5 | Which deliverable is due "next Wednesday", 2026-10-28. The board has no such date: M2 was due 2026-10-11 and M3 is due 2026-11-01. | Camden checks the syllabus. |
85	| U6 | Whether Lance agrees with any of this. Lance has reviewed **no** decision in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. | Camden talks to Lance. Until then everything is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED. |
86	
87	## 2. The product, as revised
88	
89	### 2.1 In one paragraph
90	
91	carwatch is a small plastic box with one USB-C port and one three-color light. It lives in
92	a car, plugged into whatever USB-C charger the owner already has. When the car powers
93	the charger the box boots, listens to the car's engine sensors through a Bluetooth OBD2
94	dongle, records everything to a crash-safe log, learns what *this car's* normal looks like
95	at each operating point, and flags behavior that leaves it, naming the likely fault area.
96	When the car shuts off, power disappears; the box notices, finishes its writes on a small
97	amount of stored energy, and halts cleanly, then sits off until the next start. A phone
98	joins the box's own Wi-Fi to see status and trends and to download a report that says
99	what is wrong with the box or the car. The claim we defend (D-021, to be reworded to "the
100	car it is installed in" by D-022): *it learns that car's normal across its Mode 01 engine
101	sensors, flags behavior outside it, and names the likely fault area, with measured catch
102	and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.* Not "predicts failure."
103	
104	### 2.2 The physical product
105	
106	| Item | Specification |
107	| --- | --- |
108	| Shell | Heat-resistant plastic (a cabin sits well above 60 °C parked in sun; ordinary PLA softens near 60 °C, so use ABS, ASA or similar, to be confirmed against the shell's datasheet). **No metal around the Pi's antenna**: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi share one radio. Vent slots on the top and bottom for passive airflow. Target envelope on the order of 95 × 65 × 30 mm for a Pi 4 plus the power board (estimate, to be confirmed against real parts). A food-container prototype is acceptable per the handout; the sleek shell is the product intent. |
109	| Power port | One USB-C receptacle. The only power input. Wired as a plain **sink** (5.1 kΩ resistors on both CC pins) so any source offers 5 V only. |
110	| Light | One tri-color LED visible through the shell. See §2.3. |
111	| Buttons | None. |
112	| Other ports | None. The OBD2 dongle is a separate item in the car's OBD2 port and reaches the box over Bluetooth, so no wire of ours touches it. |
113	| Install | Plug the dongle into the OBD2 port, plug the box into any USB-C charger in the car. Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped. |
114	| Inside | Raspberry Pi 4, microSD, a power block (§3.1), the light, and nothing else on the header. |
115	| Not supported | A power source that stays live with the key off. The box is designed for power that disappears when the car turns off; on an always-live port it would simply stay on. This is an installation requirement, written down as a limitation, not a mode to engineer around. |
116	
117	### 2.3 The light
118	
119	One tri-color LED on three GPIOs (each through its own resistor; value to be set by the
120	schematic against the chosen LED's datasheet). Written **only by the supervisor** (the
121	rule from D-014, kept).
122	
123	| Color and pattern | Meaning |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| Green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go. |
126	| Yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: starting up through a supply dip, or shutting down. |
127	| Red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** the car. The report says which. |
128	| Steady any color, or dark while the car is on | The device is hung or not running. Never a valid live state. |
129	| Dark while the car is off | Normal. The box is powered down. |
130	
131	Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green.
132	
133	**Why every live state pulses.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process that drove
134	it dies. A steady green would freeze into a false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If
135	every live state blinks or pulses, a frozen light of any color can only mean "not
136	running." This is D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors. Camden said to choose
137	whichever is safer, and this is.
138	
139	**Open (§11):** what the light shows during the roughly 20 to 40 seconds the Pi spends
140	booting, when no software can drive it yet. Recommendation R4: hold the yellow LED on in
141	hardware from power-up until the supervisor takes over the GPIOs, so *steady yellow* means
142	"booting, not yet running," consistent with the rule above.
143	
144	**What counts as red** (the supervisor sets it; the report explains it):
145	
146	- Box: a child process is down or restart-limited; the adapter has been silent while the
147	  engine is running; storage is failing or the disk is nearly full; undervoltage
148	  (`vcgencmd get_throttled` non-zero) or thermal throttling; the stored-energy element
149	  failed its self-check.
150	- Car: a verdict has surfaced after hysteresis and dwell (D.3): a fault
151	  area was named. A sensor the car stopped answering is also a car-side event.
152	
153	### 2.4 What the box does in a drive (behavior, end to end)
154	
155	1. The owner starts the car. The charger energizes. The box begins charging its stored
156	   energy and boots the Pi (light per §2.3).
157	2. `supervisor` starts `obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and the status-page server, each
158	   supervised (mechanism E). A heartbeat appears within 60 seconds.
159	3. `obdd` finds the Bluetooth dongle at `/dev/obd`, initializes it, and round-robins Mode
160	   01 requests (D-012). Samples go through the shared-memory ring (B.3, refuse-don't-
161	   overwrite) to `storaged`, which writes them in committed batches (D-025).
162	4. `analyzed` bins by operating point, updates per-bin statistics, computes Mahalanobis
163	   residuals and Theil–Sen trends, classifies, and runs the state machine with hysteresis
164	   and dwell. Verdicts surface only after dwell.
165	5. The light goes green once everything is up.
166	6. The car turns off. Power disappears. The box detects it, waits out the grace period
167	   (R2), then: stops capture, commits the final batch, writes a checkpoint, syncs, and
168	   halts the Pi (light yellow). The power stage then removes the Pi's supply and the box
169	   is dark.
170	7. If anything goes wrong in step 6 (stored energy empty, cable pulled, source returns
171	   mid-shutdown), the crash-consistent log still recovers at the next boot (D-025). The
172	   clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.
173	8. At the next start the cycle repeats and the box reports in its log whether the previous
174	   session ended cleanly or was recovered.
175	
176	### 2.5 The phone
177	
178	- The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi access point with WPA2, a per-device passphrase, and **no
179	  upstream and no internet** (D-013). The phone joins it. The product has no cloud.
180	- A read-only status page shows status, current verdicts and trends. A **Download report**
181	  button returns the report (R3). Nothing on the page can change the device, except the
182	  clock question in §11 (R5).
183	- A native app is a stretch and is not planned for M2 to M5. The page works on any phone.
184	- **The box is off when the car is off, so the phone can reach it only while the car
185	  is running or while the box is plugged into any charger at home.** This is a property
186	  of the product (P8), and it should be written in the README as a feature: plug it into
187	  a phone charger at home and it boots and serves the same page.
188	- `obdctl` remains the primary, exact interface with its five verbs (D-013 and the
189	  handout's "crisp CLI" guidance). Any graded behavior must be demonstrable through
190	  `obdctl` alone.
191	
192	**Report contents (proposal, to be finalized in board item `reportspec`):**
193	
194	| Section | Content |
195	| --- | --- |
196	| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy (the Pi has no battery-backed clock), `src` mix of the data (live, replay, synth: always labeled) |
197	| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
198	| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, stored-energy self-check, storage free space |
199	| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, which sensors cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
200	| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
201	| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |
202	
203	### 2.6 The 48-hour soak, under the professor's definition (P3)
204	
205	Not 48 continuous powered hours. A **48-hour wall-clock window of normal use** in which:
206	
207	- the box powers on at every key-on, records, and shuts down at every key-off;
208	- every drive shows a timestamped boot, hourly heartbeats while running (the Pi is off
209	  while parked, so the log shows deliberate gaps; this needs the professor's written okay,
210	  U4), and an orderly end of each session;
211	- **at least one injected fault** (unplug the OBD2 dongle for ten minutes while the engine
212	  is running, or `kill -9` a child) with detection, degradation and recovery visible;
213	- the key-off power loss counts as each session's end, and the log proves whether it was a
214	  clean shutdown or a recovery.
215	
216	The raw logs are the deliverable and are never tidied (`soak/README.md`). Because the soak
217	now needs a real car, the fake OBD2 port (`obdsim`) is a development tool only, never the
218	soak's data source. Leave margin to run the soak twice.
219	
220	## 3. Engineering specification
221	
222	All numbers marked **(E)** are Claude's estimates from general knowledge, **not
223	measurements**, and must be replaced by measured values before they appear in
224	`docs/DESIGN.md` as anything but "estimate". `CLAUDE.md` §8.4: a measured voltage beats an
225	opinion.
226	
227	### 3.1 The power block
228	
229	```text
230	 any USB-C source ─▶ [CC sink, 5.1 kΩ x2] ─▶ [input protection] ─▶ [current limit,
231	                                                                    inrush control]
232	                                                                           │
233	                                  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┤
234	                                  ▼                                        ▼
235	                      [stored-energy element        [power-path: source first, stored
236	                       + balancing + fuse]  ◀──────  energy fills only the gap]
237	                                                                           │
238	                                                          [5 V, 3 A converter] ─▶ Pi 4
239	   "source present" ─▶ GPIO (shutdown trigger)        "halt done" ◀── GPIO (cut the converter)
240	```
241	
242	**Requirements** (each becomes a line in `docs/hardware/wiring.md` with a measurement):
243	
244	1. **Sink only, 5 V only.** A dumb sink never negotiates above 5 V, so no source can
245	   offer the Pi more than 5 V. Add transient and reverse-polarity protection and a fuse.
246	2. **Input current limit** below the source's rating, and an **inrush limiter**: an empty
247	   stored-energy element looks like a short circuit and would trip a modest source.
248	3. **Power-path behavior:** the source feeds the Pi first; the stored energy covers only
249	   the shortfall (weak source) or the gap (crank dip, source loss).
250	4. **Source-present signal** on a GPIO, so the supervisor can detect power loss.
251	5. **Halt-done signal:** when the Pi has finished halting, the power stage removes the
252	   converter output so the box goes fully dark and the stored energy is not wasted. The Pi
253	   can drive a GPIO low at poweroff (the `gpio-poweroff` device-tree overlay); confirm on
254	   the board.
255	6. **Auto power-on:** when the source returns, the converter must enable again without a
256	   button. This is how "auto boots on the next start" is satisfied.
257	7. **Stored energy bounded by design:** the element is sized so that stored runtime is
258	   on the order of tens of seconds and never approaches a minute at the Pi's load (P8).
259	
260	**Sizing sketch (E, to be replaced by measurement):**
261	
262	| Quantity | Estimate |
263	| --- | --- |
264	| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | about 3 to 5 W |
265	| Clean-shutdown energy | 10 to 15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50 to 70 J |
266	| Crank-bridge energy | 1 to 3 s × 5 W ≈ 5 to 15 J |
267	| A bank of two series 2.7 V supercapacitor cells, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored, about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor |
268	| Charging time from empty at a 1 A budget | C·ΔV ÷ I ≈ 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s |
269	
270	**Consequence the next session must not forget:** a 10 F bank needs on the order of a
271	minute to charge at 1 A. A smaller bank charges faster; a weaker source charges slower.
272	At a **cold start the bank is empty**, so it cannot bridge the crank dip on the first
273	start of a session, and the Pi may reset during cranking. That is survivable only because
274	of the crash-consistent log (D-025). The clean-shutdown path at key-off is reliable (the
275	bank has had a whole drive to charge); the crank-bridge path at key-on is best-effort and
276	must be described honestly in the design document. Measure it before claiming it.
277	
278	**Why a supercapacitor (R1) rather than a lithium cell.** Lithium cells must not charge
279	above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window on both ends (a
280	Colorado winter and a parked summer afternoon). Many cheap Pi UPS boards have no
281	temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no thermal-runaway failure mode, tolerates a wide
282	temperature range (confirm against the part's datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job
283	exactly. Its costs are low voltage per cell (so two in series, with balancing), very low
284	internal resistance (so it needs a fuse), and a fast self-discharge that does not matter
285	for a box that is off at rest. If Camden prefers a cell anyway: use LiFePO4 or a charger
286	with a temperature-sense input that inhibits charging outside the safe window, a protected
287	cell, and a physical position away from the Pi's heat. Whichever is chosen, **a part
288	number goes into the BOM only with its datasheet linked and a human having checked it**
289	(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4; Claude cannot see the board).
290	
291	**Mechanical and thermal:** a Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C. Cabin heat plus a sealed shell
292	is the likeliest way to hit that. Specify a heatsink, vents, and a measured temperature
293	in a hot parked car (board item `thermal`). Supercapacitor and SD-card temperature ratings
294	must cover the cabin's range.
295	
296	### 3.2 Power-event state machine (the supervisor's, mechanism E)
297	
298	| State | Entered when | The supervisor does | Light |
299	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
300	| `BOOTING` | Linux up, supervisor starts | Starts children, waits for first heartbeats | steady yellow until it owns the GPIOs (R4), then open: D-027 reserves yellow blink for stored energy (`ledspec`) |

# Revision plan: the box redesign and the road to M2

> **STATUS: PROPOSAL, written 2026-10-21 in Camden's session. Nothing in this file is a
> decision.** A decision exists only when it is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` as
> ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, in the same commit as whatever enacts it, and signed later by a human.
> Claude never marks a decision reviewed or 🔒 LOCKED (`CLAUDE.md` §0).
>
> **Update, later on 2026-10-21: stage 1 is done** on branch `camden/m2/revision-plan`.
> D-022 to D-031 are in `docs/DECISIONS.md` as ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, with every dependent doc
> edit. Where this file and `DECISIONS.md` disagree, `DECISIONS.md` wins. What was
> answered, and what is still open, is marked in §1.2, §4.2 and §11.
>
> **Audience: a fresh Claude session with no memory of the conversation that produced this
> file.** Everything it needs is here or named by path. Where this file says "Camden
> decided", that is a statement about the 2026-10-21 conversation, and §1 says exactly
> which statements those are. Everything else is Claude's recommendation and must be
> confirmed with Camden before it is written down as settled.

## 0. How to use this file

1. Do the session-start steps in `CLAUDE.md` §0 first (read `docs/milestones.md`, the
   review queue at the top of `docs/DECISIONS.md`, run the board status, check `git
   status` is clean, `git pull`, create a branch **before** the first edit).
2. Read §1 (provenance), then §2 and §3 (the product and its engineering numbers), then
   §4 (what is wrong in the repo today).
3. Work through §8 in order. Each stage is one pull request; each commit inside it is one
   responsibility (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3). Do not skip ahead: later stages assume the earlier
   decisions exist.
4. Stop and ask Camden at every item in §11. Do not guess at them.
5. Obey §12 (the do-not list) at all times.
6. At the end of the session do the `CLAUDE.md` §0 end steps, including the transcript
   copy-out (`partners/camden/transcripts/README.md` now has the macOS command).

This plan edits documents first and code later. No money is spent by anything in it
(§10). Camden's standing instruction: be very sure of the paper plan before any part is
bought.

## 1. Provenance: what Camden decided, and what Claude only recommended

### 1.1 Decided by Camden in the 2026-10-21 conversation

| # | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| P1 | The team's 2008 Subaru Forester (non-turbo, Camden's car) is a testbed. Lance's 2015 Honda CR-V remains Lance's to use. **Neither car is required of anyone, and no document may restrict where either partner tests.** Camden's instruction, paraphrased: do not set limitations or restrictions for him, and especially not for Lance while the two of them are not communicating. |
| P2 | Tasks have no pre-assigned owners. Any open task is for whoever is available. For the handout's per-subsystem map, Camden chose **claim on first commit**: whoever lands a subsystem's first substantive commit is recorded as its owner. |
| P3 | The professor said the 48-hour soak means **48 hours of regular use** (not 48 hours powered): the car starts and stops, the product handles every cycle, is on and working every time the car runs, shuts down gracefully when the car shuts off, and auto-boots on the next start. Camden chose the reading "48 hours wall-clock of normal use". This has **not** been received in writing. |
| P4 | Camden approved **extending locked decision C.1** (append-only, CRC'd records) with write-ahead-log style transactions and checkpoints: a batch is `BEGIN`, records, `COMMIT`; recovery redoes committed work from the latest checkpoint and undoes uncommitted work. Camden's reason: it ties the project to the logging and checkpoint techniques taught in class. |
| P5 | `pisensor` (an MPU-6050 or similar on the Pi for mechanisms B and F) is **declined**. Mechanisms D and E stay the committed pair. |
| P6 | The Raspberry Pi 4 stays (both partners already own one). |
| P7 | **The product is one box.** The box has a single clean USB-C port (like a computer's) as its only power input. The user plugs in whatever USB-C charger and cable they already own. Camden: "no need to reinvent the charger." The team designs the box; the team buys only the OBD2 Bluetooth dongle and a cable. The box limits what any source can push, and supplements weak power from a small stored-energy element. |
| P8 | The stored-energy element is **small and short-lived by design**: its jobs are supplementing weak input power, bridging the dip at engine start, and giving the Pi enough time for a clean shutdown. It is **never** an always-on source and is not to be designed as one; about one minute of stored runtime is the ceiling and a few seconds to tens of seconds is the goal. The Pi is **intentionally off at rest**, which is what makes the 48-hour soak definition (P3) valid. |
| P9 | The Bluetooth OBD2 dongle is assumed to work as expected (Bluetooth Classic serial profile, **not BLE**). The box reads it, logs, and processes the data. |
| P10 | **Wake button: dropped.** The box has one port and one light and no buttons. |
| P11 | **One tri-color light.** Red means an issue, and "issue" means either a problem with the box or a problem with the car; the report says which. Yellow means starting or stopping on stored energy. Green means ready, all systems go. For pulse versus steady, Camden said whichever is safer, so §2.3 specifies pulsing. |
| P12 | The phone connects to the box (its own Wi-Fi) to view data and trends and to **download a report**. An app is "maybe": a stretch, not a commitment. |
| P13 | The box is "super small, sleek", with vents if needed. |
| P14 | **No shopping for now.** The paper plan comes first. |

### 1.2 Recommended by Claude, not confirmed by Camden (confirm before recording)

| # | Recommendation | Why it is still open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | The stored-energy element is a **supercapacitor bank**, not a lithium cell. | Camden said "small rechargeable battery" first, then described the seconds-scale role. He never chose the chemistry. §3.1 has the reasoning (no thermal runaway, no charge-temperature cutoff to design, works in a hot or frozen car). |
| R2 | A **short grace period** after the source disappears, longer than a crank dip and shorter than the stored runtime, before shutdown starts. | Needs the Forester's real supply-dip measurement. |
| R3 | **Report as one HTML file plus a CSV**, served by a C program in `src/interface/`. | Camden said "report" and "maybe an app". Format is unchosen. |
| R4 | Steady yellow while booting (a not-yet-running state), pulses everywhere once alive. | See §2.3 and §11. |
| R5 | The phone page may set the Pi's clock (the Pi has no battery-backed clock). | Conflicts with D-013's "writes nothing". §11. |
| R6 | Record the Forester as the car the first baseline and fault captures run on. | Follows from P1 but is not itself a decision about Lance. |

**Answered by Camden, 2026-10-21, and recorded:** R1 supercapacitor (D-024). R3 HTML plus
CSV served by C (D-028). R4 steady yellow held in hardware (D-027). R5 no: a real-time
clock keeps the time instead, and the page stays read-only (D-030). **Still open:** R2,
the grace period's length, which needs `cranklog`. R6 was not recorded: P1 says no car is
required, so D-022 names both cars and neither as first.

### 1.3 Unknown, must be measured or asked

| # | Unknown | How to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U1 | Which Mode 01 PIDs the Forester answers, and its OBD protocol. A 2008 US car is expected to speak CAN (ISO 15765-4) but this is **not verified**. MAP may be absent. | PID survey (§8, stage 3). Do not assume; the sensor list and fault areas depend on it. |
| U2 | The Forester's supply behavior at crank, and whether its sockets and ports switch with the key. | Meter. Free first test: a USB charger with a light in the socket, key off. |
| U3 | Real Pi 4 boot and shutdown time and power draw on this image. | USB-C power meter and `systemd-analyze`. |
| U4 | The professor's written confirmation of the soak definition (P3). | Email, drafted in §9. Camden sends it. |
| U5 | Which deliverable is due "next Wednesday", 2026-10-28. The board has no such date: M2 was due 2026-10-11 and M3 is due 2026-11-01. | Camden checks the syllabus. |
| U6 | Whether Lance agrees with any of this. Lance has reviewed **no** decision in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. | Camden talks to Lance. Until then everything is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED. |

## 2. The product, as revised

### 2.1 In one paragraph

carwatch is a small plastic box with one USB-C port and one three-color light. It lives in
a car, plugged into whatever USB-C charger the owner already has. When the car powers
the charger the box boots, listens to the car's engine sensors through a Bluetooth OBD2
dongle, records everything to a crash-safe log, learns what *this car's* normal looks like
at each operating point, and flags behavior that leaves it, naming the likely fault area.
When the car shuts off, power disappears; the box notices, finishes its writes on a small
amount of stored energy, and halts cleanly, then sits off until the next start. A phone
joins the box's own Wi-Fi to see status and trends and to download a report that says
what is wrong with the box or the car. The claim we defend (D-021, to be reworded to "the
car it is installed in" by D-022): *it learns that car's normal across its Mode 01 engine
sensors, flags behavior outside it, and names the likely fault area, with measured catch
and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.* Not "predicts failure."

### 2.2 The physical product

| Item | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Shell | Heat-resistant plastic (a cabin sits well above 60 °C parked in sun; ordinary PLA softens near 60 °C, so use ABS, ASA or similar, to be confirmed against the shell's datasheet). **No metal around the Pi's antenna**: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi share one radio. Vent slots on the top and bottom for passive airflow. Target envelope on the order of 95 × 65 × 30 mm for a Pi 4 plus the power board (estimate, to be confirmed against real parts). A food-container prototype is acceptable per the handout; the sleek shell is the product intent. |
| Power port | One USB-C receptacle. The only power input. Wired as a plain **sink** (5.1 kΩ resistors on both CC pins) so any source offers 5 V only. |
| Light | One tri-color LED visible through the shell. See §2.3. |
| Buttons | None. |
| Other ports | None. The OBD2 dongle is a separate item in the car's OBD2 port and reaches the box over Bluetooth, so no wire of ours touches it. |
| Install | Plug the dongle into the OBD2 port, plug the box into any USB-C charger in the car. Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped. |
| Inside | Raspberry Pi 4, microSD, a power block (§3.1), the light, and nothing else on the header. |
| Not supported | A power source that stays live with the key off. The box is designed for power that disappears when the car turns off; on an always-live port it would simply stay on. This is an installation requirement, written down as a limitation, not a mode to engineer around. |

### 2.3 The light

One tri-color LED on three GPIOs (each through its own resistor; value to be set by the
schematic against the chosen LED's datasheet). Written **only by the supervisor** (the
rule from D-014, kept).

| Color and pattern | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go. |
| Yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: starting up through a supply dip, or shutting down. |
| Red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** the car. The report says which. |
| Steady any color, or dark while the car is on | The device is hung or not running. Never a valid live state. |
| Dark while the car is off | Normal. The box is powered down. |

Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green.

**Why every live state pulses.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process that drove
it dies. A steady green would freeze into a false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If
every live state blinks or pulses, a frozen light of any color can only mean "not
running." This is D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors. Camden said to choose
whichever is safer, and this is.

**Open (§11):** what the light shows during the roughly 20 to 40 seconds the Pi spends
booting, when no software can drive it yet. Recommendation R4: hold the yellow LED on in
hardware from power-up until the supervisor takes over the GPIOs, so *steady yellow* means
"booting, not yet running," consistent with the rule above.

**What counts as red** (the supervisor sets it; the report explains it):

- Box: a child process is down or restart-limited; the adapter has been silent while the
  engine is running; storage is failing or the disk is nearly full; undervoltage
  (`vcgencmd get_throttled` non-zero) or thermal throttling; the stored-energy element
  failed its self-check.
- Car: a verdict has surfaced after hysteresis and dwell (D.3): a fault
  area was named. A sensor the car stopped answering is also a car-side event.

### 2.4 What the box does in a drive (behavior, end to end)

1. The owner starts the car. The charger energizes. The box begins charging its stored
   energy and boots the Pi (light per §2.3).
2. `supervisor` starts `obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and the status-page server, each

3. `obdd` finds the Bluetooth dongle at `/dev/obd`, initializes it, and round-robins Mode
   01 requests (D-012). Samples go through the shared-memory ring (B.3, refuse-don't-
   overwrite) to `storaged`, which writes them in committed batches (D-025).

   residuals and Theil–Sen trends, classifies, and runs the state machine with hysteresis

5. The light goes green once everything is up.

   (R2), then: stops capture, commits the final batch, writes a checkpoint, syncs, and
   halts the Pi (light yellow). The power stage then removes the Pi's supply and the box
   is dark.

   mid-shutdown), the crash-consistent log still recovers at the next boot (D-025). The
   clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.
8. At the next start the cycle repeats and the box reports in its log whether the previous
   session ended cleanly or was recovered.

  upstream and no internet** (D-013). The phone joins it. The product has no cloud.
- A read-only status page shows status, current verdicts and trends. A **Download report**
  button returns the report (R3). Nothing on the page can change the device, except the
  clock question in §11 (R5).
- A native app is a stretch and is not planned for M2 to M5. The page works on any phone.
- **The box is off when the car is off, so the phone can reach it only while the car
  is running or while the box is plugged into any charger at home.** This is a property
  of the product (P8), and it should be written in the README as a feature: plug it into
  a phone charger at home and it boots and serves the same page.
- `obdctl` remains the primary, exact interface with its five verbs (D-013 and the
  handout's "crisp CLI" guidance). Any graded behavior must be demonstrable through
  `obdctl` alone.

**Report contents (proposal, to be finalized in board item `reportspec`):**

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy (the Pi has no battery-backed clock), `src` mix of the data (live, replay, synth: always labeled) |
| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, stored-energy self-check, storage free space |
| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, which sensors cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |

- the box powers on at every key-on, records, and shuts down at every key-off;
- every drive shows a timestamped boot, hourly heartbeats while running (the Pi is off
  while parked, so the log shows deliberate gaps; this needs the professor's written okay,

  clean shutdown or a recovery.

now needs a real car, the fake OBD2 port (`obdsim`) is a development tool only, never the
soak's data source. Leave margin to run the soak twice.

## 3. Engineering specification

All numbers marked **(E)** are Claude's estimates from general knowledge, **not
measurements**, and must be replaced by measured values before they appear in

opinion.

### 3.1 The power block

```text
 any USB-C source ─▶ [CC sink, 5.1 kΩ x2] ─▶ [input protection] ─▶ [current limit,
                                                                    inrush control]
                                                                           │
                                  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┤
                                  ▼                                        ▼
                      [stored-energy element        [power-path: source first, stored
                       + balancing + fuse]  ◀──────  energy fills only the gap]
                                                                           │
                                                          [5 V, 3 A converter] ─▶ Pi 4
   "source present" ─▶ GPIO (shutdown trigger)        "halt done" ◀── GPIO (cut the converter)
```

**Requirements** (each becomes a line in `docs/hardware/wiring.md` with a measurement):

1. **Sink only, 5 V only.** A dumb sink never negotiates above 5 V, so no source can
   offer the Pi more than 5 V. Add transient and reverse-polarity protection and a fuse.
2. **Input current limit** below the source's rating, and an **inrush limiter**: an empty
   stored-energy element looks like a short circuit and would trip a modest source.
3. **Power-path behavior:** the source feeds the Pi first; the stored energy covers only
   the shortfall (weak source) or the gap (crank dip, source loss).
4. **Source-present signal** on a GPIO, so the supervisor can detect power loss.
5. **Halt-done signal:** when the Pi has finished halting, the power stage removes the
   converter output so the box goes fully dark and the stored energy is not wasted. The Pi
   can drive a GPIO low at poweroff (the `gpio-poweroff` device-tree overlay); confirm on
   the board.
6. **Auto power-on:** when the source returns, the converter must enable again without a
   button. This is how "auto boots on the next start" is satisfied.
7. **Stored energy bounded by design:** the element is sized so that stored runtime is
   on the order of tens of seconds and never approaches a minute at the Pi's load (P8).

**Sizing sketch (E, to be replaced by measurement):**

| Quantity | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | about 3 to 5 W |
| Clean-shutdown energy | 10 to 15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50 to 70 J |
| Crank-bridge energy | 1 to 3 s × 5 W ≈ 5 to 15 J |
| A bank of two series 2.7 V supercapacitor cells, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored, about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor |
| Charging time from empty at a 1 A budget | C·ΔV ÷ I ≈ 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s |

**Consequence the next session must not forget:** a 10 F bank needs on the order of a
minute to charge at 1 A. A smaller bank charges faster; a weaker source charges slower.
At a **cold start the bank is empty**, so it cannot bridge the crank dip on the first
start of a session, and the Pi may reset during cranking. That is survivable only because
of the crash-consistent log (D-025). The clean-shutdown path at key-off is reliable (the
bank has had a whole drive to charge); the crank-bridge path at key-on is best-effort and
must be described honestly in the design document. Measure it before claiming it.

**Why a supercapacitor (R1) rather than a lithium cell.** Lithium cells must not charge
above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window on both ends (a
Colorado winter and a parked summer afternoon). Many cheap Pi UPS boards have no
temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no thermal-runaway failure mode, tolerates a wide
temperature range (confirm against the part's datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job
exactly. Its costs are low voltage per cell (so two in series, with balancing), very low
internal resistance (so it needs a fuse), and a fast self-discharge that does not matter
for a box that is off at rest. If Camden prefers a cell anyway: use LiFePO4 or a charger
with a temperature-sense input that inhibits charging outside the safe window, a protected
cell, and a physical position away from the Pi's heat. Whichever is chosen, **a part
number goes into the BOM only with its datasheet linked and a human having checked it**
(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4; Claude cannot see the board).

**Mechanical and thermal:** a Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C. Cabin heat plus a sealed shell
is the likeliest way to hit that. Specify a heatsink, vents, and a measured temperature
in a hot parked car (board item `thermal`). Supercapacitor and SD-card temperature ratings
must cover the cabin's range.

| `BOOTING` | Linux up, supervisor starts | Starts children, waits for first heartbeats | steady yellow until it owns the GPIOs (R4), then open: D-027 reserves yellow blink for stored energy (`ledspec`) |

313	### 3.3 Storage: write-ahead transactions and checkpoints (mechanism D, D-025)
314	
315	This extends 🔒 C.1; it does not remove any of its rules. Records stay append-only,
316	self-framing (magic), and CRC'd over the whole record, and every record keeps its `src`
317	tag (C.2).
318	
319	- **Transaction.** `storaged` drains the ring into a batch: `BEGIN(txn_id)`, the sample
320	  records, `COMMIT(txn_id)`, then one `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT`
321	  is on disk.
322	- **Checkpoint.** Periodically (rarely, to keep the write load and memory low), write a
323	  snapshot of the learned baselines plus the log offset and last committed `txn_id` it
324	  covers. Use **two alternating slots (A/B)**, each CRC'd and carrying a generation
325	  counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut can never destroy the previous good one.
326	- **Recovery at boot.** Load the newest valid checkpoint. Scan the log forward from its
327	  offset, verifying every CRC. **Redo**: re-apply every committed transaction to the
328	  baselines. **Undo**: any transaction with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN`; the
329	  scan stops at the first bad CRC and truncates the torn tail. Log exactly what was
330	  recovered and what was lost (counts and offsets).
331	- **Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (that is C.1's
332	  point), so there is no before-image to restore. State this plainly in the design
333	  document and at the defense; do not claim an undo log the design does not need.
334	- **Record format proposal (decision `recfmt`, to be confirmed):** add kinds
335	  `REC_TXN_BEGIN`, `REC_TXN_COMMIT`, `REC_CHECKPOINT` and `REC_BOOT` to `rec_kind_t` in
336	  `include/store/record.h`; add a `boot_id` to the header (there is a spare 16-bit field
337	  today; a 32-bit `boot_id` needs a layout change, so bump `REC_VERSION` to 2 and keep the
338	  known-answer CRC test unchanged); every session starts with a `REC_BOOT` record that
339	  states whether the previous session ended cleanly.
340	- **fsync policy (provisional, `fsync`):** one commit and one `fsync` per batch of about
341	  one second. Records are about 48 bytes (a 40-byte header plus a small payload, E), the
342	  request budget is about 10 to 20 per second (D-012), so about 1 KB/s, about 3.5 MB per
343	  hour of running, and on the order of 170 MB over 48 *running* hours (the 48 hour
344	  *wall-clock* soak records far less because the box is off while parked). The worst loss
345	  from a power cut that beats the clean shutdown is about one second of samples, which
346	  holds nothing a user would miss. The argument for the batch size must be written in
347	  `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 before the code is written (C.1's standing instruction).
348	- **Baseline persistence:** learned per-bin statistics are the model's state, so they must
349	  survive every key cycle. Checkpoint plus replay since the checkpoint is exactly how.
350	- **Clock:** the Pi has no battery-backed clock. Every record carries `mono_ns` and a
351	  `boot_id`; wall time is best-effort. Raspberry Pi OS ships `fake-hwclock`, which saves
352	  the time at a clean shutdown and restores it at boot, so a clean shutdown also keeps the
353	  clock close. Verify on the image.

### 3.3 Storage: write-ahead transactions and checkpoints (mechanism D, D-025)

This extends 🔒 C.1; it does not remove any of its rules. Records stay append-only,
self-framing (magic), and CRC'd over the whole record, and every record keeps its `src`
tag (C.2).

- **Transaction.** `storaged` drains the ring into a batch: `BEGIN(txn_id)`, the sample
  records, `COMMIT(txn_id)`, then one `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT`
  is on disk.
- **Checkpoint.** Periodically (rarely, to keep the write load and memory low), write a
  snapshot of the learned baselines plus the log offset and last committed `txn_id` it
  covers. Use **two alternating slots (A/B)**, each CRC'd and carrying a generation
  counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut can never destroy the previous good one.
- **Recovery at boot.** Load the newest valid checkpoint. Scan the log forward from its
  offset, verifying every CRC. **Redo**: re-apply every committed transaction to the
  baselines. **Undo**: any transaction with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN`; the
  scan stops at the first bad CRC and truncates the torn tail. Log exactly what was
  recovered and what was lost (counts and offsets).
- **Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (that is C.1's
  point), so there is no before-image to restore. State this plainly in the design
  document and at the defense; do not claim an undo log the design does not need.
- **Record format proposal (decision `recfmt`, to be confirmed):** add kinds
  `REC_TXN_BEGIN`, `REC_TXN_COMMIT`, `REC_CHECKPOINT` and `REC_BOOT` to `rec_kind_t` in
  `include/store/record.h`; add a `boot_id` to the header (there is a spare 16-bit field
  today; a 32-bit `boot_id` needs a layout change, so bump `REC_VERSION` to 2 and keep the
  known-answer CRC test unchanged); every session starts with a `REC_BOOT` record that
  states whether the previous session ended cleanly.
- **fsync policy (provisional, `fsync`):** one commit and one `fsync` per batch of about
  one second. Records are about 48 bytes (a 40-byte header plus a small payload, E), the
  request budget is about 10 to 20 per second (D-012), so about 1 KB/s, about 3.5 MB per
  hour of running, and on the order of 170 MB over 48 *running* hours (the 48 hour
  *wall-clock* soak records far less because the box is off while parked). The worst loss
  from a power cut that beats the clean shutdown is about one second of samples, which
  holds nothing a user would miss. The argument for the batch size must be written in
  `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 before the code is written (C.1's standing instruction).
- **Baseline persistence:** learned per-bin statistics are the model's state, so they must
  survive every key cycle. Checkpoint plus replay since the checkpoint is exactly how.
- **Clock:** the Pi has no battery-backed clock. Every record carries `mono_ns` and a
  `boot_id`; wall time is best-effort. Raspberry Pi OS ships `fake-hwclock`, which saves
  the time at a clean shutdown and restores it at boot, so a clean shutdown also keeps the
  clock close. Verify on the image.

### 3.4 The boot-time budget

A stock Pi 4 takes roughly 25 to 40 seconds to boot (E), and Camden's "a few seconds" is
not achievable without a trimmed image. The Forester's cooling warm-up is the most
informative part of a drive, so a lost first half-minute is a real cost: the design
document's substitutions section must say so. Mitigations to measure (board items
`bootbudget`, `bootimg`): disable unused services, `systemd-analyze blame`, start `obdd`
as early as possible, and let capture begin before the phone Wi-Fi is up.

Rules (`CLAUDE.md` §7.11, `docs/BOARD/BOARD.md`): edit lines, then run `python3
tools/board_sync.py` (it needs Python 3.11 or newer; the Makefile picks one for you).
**Never** type or change a `<!-- #n -->` tag. **Claude never ticks a question, decision or
hardware line**; where this plan says "cut", the *human* ticks the box and adds "(cut)".
Remove the `@camden` and `@lance` markers from every line (P2); run `--check` first to see
whether sync removes the assignee, and tell Camden if it does not.

### 7.1 Lines to retitle or reword (keep the slug)

| `obdsim` | M3 tools: fake OBD2 port for development, labeled synth (never the soak's source) |

| `evalplan` | M2 docs: evaluation plan with committed target numbers, including shutdown and recovery |

### 7.2 Lines to cut (a human ticks and adds "(cut)")

| Slug | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `soakq` | Answered by D-023 once the professor confirms in writing |
| `pisensor` | Decided by P5 and recorded as D-029 |
| `canirq`, `canpoll`, `expirq`, `expdrop` | Exist only if `pisensor` brought B and F back; declined |

| `ownmap` | Moot under D-026 |

### 7.3 Lines to add (no tags, no `@owner`)

M2:

  and VIN
- `profmail` M2 decision: get the professor's 48-hour soak definition in writing
- `powerspec` M2 docs: power worksheet: Pi draw by state, shutdown and crank energy,
  bank size
- `shutfsm` M2 docs: power-event state machine and the grace period
- `bootbudget` M2 docs: boot-time budget and what the first minute of a drive loses
- `walspec` M2 decision: write-ahead transactions and A/B checkpoints, record kinds

- `reportspec` M2 docs: report contents and format, box fault versus car fault
- `enclspec` M2 docs: box mechanical spec: size, vents, heat-rated plastic, antenna

M3:
