# carwatch — CS370 term project
# Systems core is C17 and must stay -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean (CLAUDE.md §2.4).

CC       ?= gcc

# tools/ needs tomllib, which is Python 3.11+. The department machines put 3.9
# on PATH as python3, where boardcheck dies with ModuleNotFoundError before it
# can report anything useful. Pick the first interpreter that can actually parse
# the board; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, still comes from tools/.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              $$p -c 'import tomllib' >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \
            done; echo python3)
CSTD      = -std=c17
WARN      = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wvla
OPT      ?= -O2 -g
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude -D_GNU_SOURCE
CFLAGS   += $(CSTD) $(WARN) $(OPT)
LDLIBS   += -lm -lpthread

BUILD    = build
BIN      = $(BUILD)/bin

ALL_SRC    = $(wildcard src/*/*.c)
# Library objects: everything except the per-daemon entry points.
COMMON_SRC = $(filter-out %/main.c,$(ALL_SRC))
COMMON_OBJ = $(COMMON_SRC:%.c=$(BUILD)/%.o)

DAEMONS    = obdd storaged analyzed supervisor obdctl
DAEMON_BIN = $(addprefix $(BIN)/,$(DAEMONS))

TEST_SRC   = $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)
TEST_BIN   = $(TEST_SRC:tests/%.c=$(BIN)/%)

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck replay deploy clean boundary boardcheck \
        hwcheck hwdocs hwclean toolcheck

all: $(DAEMON_BIN)

$(BIN)/obdd:       $(BUILD)/src/obd/main.o        $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/storaged:   $(BUILD)/src/store/main.o      $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/analyzed:   $(BUILD)/src/analysis/main.o   $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/supervisor: $(BUILD)/src/supervisor/main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/obdctl:     $(BUILD)/src/interface/main.o  $(COMMON_OBJ)

$(DAEMON_BIN):
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

$(BIN)/test_%: tests/test_%.c $(COMMON_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

test: $(TEST_BIN) boundary boardcheck toolcheck
	@fail=0; for t in $(TEST_BIN); do \
		printf '%-28s ' "$$(basename $$t)"; \
		if $$t; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL; fail=1; fi; done; \
	exit $$fail

# CLAUDE.md §2.1 — a grader must be able to confirm the boundary in sixty seconds.
# No network client anywhere in the product except src/interface/.
boundary:
	@if grep -rnE '\b(curl_|SSL_|getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|socket)\b' src \
	     --include='*.c' --include='*.h' | grep -v '^src/interface/'; then \
		echo "BOUNDARY VIOLATION: network symbol outside src/interface/"; exit 1; \
	else echo "boundary                     PASS"; fi

# docs/milestones.md is the board (D-020) - every task, question and decision
# in the project is a checkbox there. Validate it in the same gate as the C.
boardcheck:
	@$(PY) tools/test_board.py

# Python tool tests (stdlib unittest, tests/tools/). The venv is made on first use, and
# refreshed when a requirements file changes, so a fresh clone stays green; it needs the
# network for that install. Dev only (D-032).
.venv/.installed: tools/requirements.txt tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@test -x .venv/bin/python || $(PY) -m venv .venv
	@.venv/bin/pip install -q -r tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@touch $@

toolcheck: .venv/.installed
	@PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests/tools -q && \
		echo "toolcheck                    PASS"

asan:
	$(MAKE) clean
	$(MAKE) test OPT="-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer"

memcheck: $(TEST_BIN)
	@for t in $(TEST_BIN); do valgrind --error-exitcode=1 --leak-check=full $$t || exit 1; done

soakcheck: all
	./soak/run_soak.sh --mini

replay: all
	@test -n "$(FIX)" || { echo "usage: make replay FIX=fixtures/<name>"; exit 1; }
	./tools/replay.py --fixture $(FIX) --label replay

deploy: all
	@test -n "$(PI)" || { echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@<host>"; exit 1; }
	rsync -a --exclude build --exclude .git ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- hardware
# KiCad 10. On Windows kicad-cli.exe is under
# "C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/" and is NOT on PATH by default:
#   make hwcheck KICAD="/c/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/kicad-cli.exe"
KICAD ?= kicad-cli
SCH    = electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.kicad_sch

# ERC as a build failure — the hardware equivalent of -Werror (CLAUDE.md 7.12).
hwcheck:
	@command -v $(KICAD) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { \
		echo "kicad-cli not found. Set KICAD=/path/to/kicad-cli"; exit 1; }
	$(KICAD) sch erc --exit-code-violations --format json \
	         -o electricalDrawing/erc.json $(SCH)
	@echo "erc                          PASS"

# Regenerate everything derived from the schematic. Never hand-edit the outputs.
hwdocs:
	@mkdir -p docs/figures
	$(KICAD) sch export svg --exclude-drawing-sheet -o docs/figures/ $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export bom \
	         --fields "Reference,Value,Footprint,MPN,Datasheet,Qty" \
	         --group-by Value -o docs/hardware/bom.csv $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export netlist -o electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net $(SCH)
	@echo "Regenerated: schematic SVG, bom.csv, netlist."
	@echo "Commit the SVG — PRs touching hw must show a picture."

hwclean:
	rm -f electricalDrawing/erc.json electricalDrawing/drc.json

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

input.content:
M2 build: build the sanitizer variant in build/asan so plain make still links

WHAT:   `make asan` now runs `make test` with BUILD=build/asan instead of cleaning
        and rebuilding build/ with sanitizer flags; `make clean` still removes
        both trees.
WHY:    Objects do not depend on the flags that built them, so after `make asan`
        a plain `make` linked against ASan objects and failed (undefined
        ___asan_init), and `make test` silently reran sanitized binaries
        (board item `asanbuild`, #170).
REVIEW: The `-include` of dependency files finds build/asan's .d files too; they
        only add dependency lines for build/asan targets, which is harmless.
VERIFY: make clean; make asan (exit 0); make (exit 0, was exit 2 before this
        commit); make test PASS.

M2 build: make a UBSan finding fail the asan run instead of printing PASS

WHAT:   `make asan` adds -fno-sanitize-recover=all, and a comment notes that
        LeakSanitizer runs by default on Linux but not on macOS arm64.
WHY:    UBSan reports and continues by default, so a test with undefined behavior
        printed its runtime error and still exited 0, which the test loop reports
        as PASS. Handout §13 counts sanitizer findings against the grade, so the
        gate must fail on them.
REVIEW: Checked on a one-line signed-overflow program, not by breaking a real
        test; leak checking itself is only exercised on Linux (CI, the Pi).
VERIFY: signed-overflow probe built with the old flags: exit 0; with
        -fno-sanitize-recover=all: exit 1. make clean; make asan: all PASS.

# Fault injection for the soak and for demo-day rehearsal.
#
# Demo day WILL unplug one of our sensors at a moment of their choosing. This is
# announced in the handout so that nobody can call it unfair later. Rehearse it.
set -euo pipefail

case "${1:-}" in

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Soak runner. --mini runs a 1-hour bench rehearsal (make soakcheck). The default opens
# the graded 48-hour key-cycle window (D-023): the box runs in the car as its installed
# service, and this script records the manifest and collects the session logs.
set -euo pipefail

DURATION=$((48 * 3600))
LABEL="soak"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--mini" ]]; then DURATION=3600; LABEL="mini"; fi

STAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
LOGDIR="soak/logs/${LABEL}-${STAMP}"
mkdir -p "$LOGDIR"

echo "soak: label=${LABEL} duration=${DURATION}s logdir=${LOGDIR}"
echo "soak: THE LOGS ARE THE DELIVERABLE. Do not edit them afterward."

# TODO(M3): --mini: launch build/bin/supervisor with its log to $LOGDIR/system.log
# TODO(M3): record uname -a, git rev-parse HEAD, build flags, the car, and the data
#           source (live | replay | synth) into $LOGDIR/manifest.txt BEFORE starting.
# TODO(M4): default: at the end of the window, copy the box's raw session logs into
#           $LOGDIR and list every session (boot, end, clean or recovered) in
#           $LOGDIR/sessions.txt.
# TODO(M4): record what fault was injected, when, and in which session, into
#           $LOGDIR/faults.txt
# TODO(M4): orderly end: the last session's final heartbeat; exit status recorded.

echo "not implemented — M0 scaffold" >&2
exit 1

    ap.add_argument("--fixture", required=True, help="path under fixtures/")
    ap.add_argument("--label", default="replay", choices=["replay", "synth"])
    ap.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=1.0,
                    help="1.0 = real time; >1 compresses a month into an afternoon")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    print(f"replay: fixture={args.fixture} label={args.label} speed={args.speed}x",
          file=sys.stderr)

    #           write into the same ring the live path uses, src = args.label.
    print("not implemented — M0 scaffold", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    result = {

        "t_wall": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "adapter": banner,

        "vin_hash": None,
        "model_year": None,
        "supported": [],
        "samples": {},
    }
    vin = None
    try:
        vin = ad.vin()
        result["vin_hash"] = obdlib.vin_hash(vin)
        result["model_year"] = model_year(vin)
    except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
        result["vin_error"] = str(e)
    for pid in sorted(ad.supported_pids()):
        key = f"{pid:02X}"
        result["supported"].append(key)
        try:
            data = ad.query(1, pid)
            value, unit = obdlib.decode(pid, data)
            result["samples"][key] = {"raw": data.hex(" ").upper(), "val": value,
                                      "unit": unit, "name": obdlib.pid_name(pid)}
        except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
            result["samples"][key] = {"error": str(e), "name": obdlib.pid_name(pid)}
    return result, vin


def render_markdown(r):
    lines = [
        f"### Survey {r['t_wall'][:19]}Z (`src={r['src']}`)",
        "",
        f"- Adapter: `{r['adapter']}`",
        f"- Protocol (`ATDP`): `{r['protocol']}`",
        f"- Battery (`ATRV`): `{r['voltage']}`",
        f"- VIN hash: `{r['vin_hash']}`; model year from VIN: {r['model_year']}",
        f"- Supported Mode 01 PIDs ({len(r['supported'])}): "
        + ", ".join(f"`{p}`" for p in r["supported"]),
        "",
        "| PID | Signal | Raw | Value |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for key in r["supported"]:
        s = r["samples"][key]
        value = s.get("error") or (f"{s['val']:.2f} {s['unit']}" if s["val"] is not None
                                   else "(not decoded)")
        lines.append(f"| 0x{key} | {s['name']} | `{s.get('raw', '')}` | {value} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="adapter serial port")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data", help="directory for the survey files")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        ad = elm.Adapter(args.port)
    except elm.LinkLost as e:
        print(f"pidscan: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        result, vin = scan(ad)
    except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e:
        print(f"pidscan: survey failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    finally:
        ad.close()

    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = result["t_wall"][:19].replace(":", "").replace("-", "")
    base = os.path.join(args.out, f"pidscan-{stamp}-{result['src']}")
    with open(base + ".json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(result, f, indent=2)
    md = render_markdown(result)
    with open(base + ".md", "w") as f:
        f.write(md)

    print(md)
    print(f"VIN (screen only, not saved): {vin}")
    print(f"wrote {base}.json and {base}.md")
    if result["src"] == "synth":
        print("NOTE: this adapter is obdsim. Everything above is synthetic.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('Makefile'); s=p.read_text()
a="""CC       ?= gcc

# tools/ needs tomllib, which is Python 3.11+. The department machines put 3.9
# on PATH as python3, where boardcheck dies with ModuleNotFoundError before it
# can report anything useful. Pick the first interpreter that can actually parse
# the board; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, still comes from tools/.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \\
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \\
              $$p -c 'import tomllib' >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \\
            done; echo python3)"""
b="""# CC is make's default, cc: gcc on the Pi and in CI, clang on macOS.

# OS ships; the department machines put 3.9 on PATH as python3. Pick the first interpreter
# that is new enough; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, names the version.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \\
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \\
              $$p -c 'import sys; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 11))' >/dev/null 2>&1 && \\
              { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \\
            done; echo python3)"""
assert s.count(a)==1, s[:600]; p.write_text(s.replace(a,b))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The product boundary (CLAUDE.md §2.1, D-038): a grader must confirm in sixty seconds that
# the only network code is the box's own page server. This is that confirmation.
#
#   check.sh ROOT                 check ROOT/src, ROOT/include and ROOT/Makefile
#   check.sh --selftest CASES     every CASES/bad_* must fail and every CASES/good_* pass
#
# The rules, applied to *.c and *.h, comments included:
#   1. No network family, resolver or address call outside src/interface/.
#   2. No HTTP or TLS library, no Bluetooth socket header, and no shelling out, anywhere.
#   3. socket() only in src/ipc/uds.c (Unix sockets, D-042, D-043) and src/interface/.
#   4. The Makefile links no network library.
set -uo pipefail

check() {
    local root=$1 bad=0 hits
    local dirs=()
    for d in src include; do [[ -d "$root/$d" ]] && dirs+=("$root/$d"); done

    scan() {  # scan PATTERN -> "file:line:text" for every C file under src/ and include/
        [[ ${#dirs[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0
        grep -rnE --include='*.c' --include='*.h' "$1" "${dirs[@]}" 2>/dev/null
    }
    report() {  # report RULE HITS
        [[ -z "$2" ]] && return 0
        printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed "s|^$root/||; s|^|  $1: |"
        bad=1
    }

    hits=$(scan '\b(AF|PF)_(INET6?|PACKET|NETLINK)\b|\b(getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|gethostbyaddr|getnameinfo|inet_(pton|ntop|addr|aton|ntoa))\b|#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(netdb\.h|netinet/|arpa/inet\.h)' \
           | grep -v "^$root/src/interface/")
    report "network outside src/interface/" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(curl/|openssl/|bluetooth/)|\b(curl_[a-z]|SSL_[A-Za-z])|\bAF_BLUETOOTH\b|\b(popen|system)[[:space:]]*\(')
    report "HTTP, TLS, Bluetooth socket or shell" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '\bsocket(pair)?[[:space:]]*\(' \
           | grep -v -e "^$root/src/interface/" -e "^$root/src/ipc/uds\.c:")
    report "socket() outside src/ipc/uds.c and src/interface/" "$hits"

    if [[ -f "$root/Makefile" ]]; then
        hits=$(grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(LDLIBS|LDFLAGS).*-l(curl|ssl|crypto|bluetooth)\b' "$root/Makefile" \
               | sed 's|^|Makefile:|')
        report "network library linked" "$hits"
    fi
    return $bad
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--selftest" ]]; then
    cases=${2:?usage: check.sh --selftest CASES}
    fail=0
    for c in "$cases"/bad_* "$cases"/good_*; do
        name=$(basename "$c")
        if check "$c" >/dev/null; then got=pass; else got=fail; fi
        case "$name:$got" in
            bad_*:fail|good_*:pass) ;;
            *) echo "boundary self-test: $name should not $got"; fail=1 ;;
        esac
    done
    exit $fail
fi

root=${1:?usage: check.sh ROOT | --selftest CASES}
if ! check "$root"; then
    echo "BOUNDARY VIOLATION: see CLAUDE.md §2.1 and DECISIONS D-038"
    exit 1
fi

`D-038` · Decided M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Answers:** board item `boundaryrule`

**Decision.** `make boundary`, part of `make test`, runs `tests/boundary/check.sh` over
`src/`, `include/` and the Makefile, comments included:

1. No network family, resolver or address call (`AF_INET`, `AF_INET6`, `AF_PACKET`,
   `AF_NETLINK`, `getaddrinfo`, `gethostbyname`, `inet_*`, `<netdb.h>`, `<netinet/...>`,
   `<arpa/inet.h>`) outside `src/interface/`.
2. Nowhere, the page server included: an HTTP or TLS library (`curl`, `openssl`), a
   Bluetooth socket (`AF_BLUETOOTH`, `<bluetooth/...>`), or shelling out (`system`,
   `popen`).
3. `socket()` and `socketpair()` only in `src/ipc/uds.c`, the one helper that opens Unix
   sockets (D-042, D-043), and in `src/interface/` (`statusd`).
4. No network library (`-lcurl`, `-lssl`, `-lcrypto`, `-lbluetooth`) on the link line.

Before checking the tree, it checks itself: every case in `tests/boundary/cases/bad_*`
must fail and every `good_*` must pass, so a rule that silently stops matching breaks the
build.

**Why.** The old rule banned the word `socket` outside `src/interface/`, but the design
needs Unix sockets in the supervisor, `storaged` and `analyzed` (B.2, D-042, D-043), so
the first supervisor commit would have failed `make test`, inviting someone to weaken the
check (CLAUDE.md §2.8). Its `curl_` and `SSL_` patterns could never match a real call
(both ended in `\\b` between two word characters), and it never looked at `connect`,
address families, headers, `include/` or the link line. The new rule is narrower where
the product needs room and wider everywhere else, and a grader can still read it in a
minute.

**Cost.** A text check, not a symbol check: a comment that names a banned call fails it,
which is the safe direction. It cannot prove a Unix socket is not pointed at a network
path; it relies on every socket going through one helper a reviewer can read.

---

## G. Superseded""")

M2 build: let the boundary check allow Unix sockets and test itself, as D-038

WHAT:   `make boundary` now runs tests/boundary/check.sh: no network family,
        resolver or address call outside src/interface/; no curl, openssl,
        Bluetooth socket, system() or popen() anywhere; socket() only in
        src/ipc/uds.c and src/interface/; no network library on the link line;
        include/ scanned as well as src/. It first runs its own self-test: seven
        tests/boundary/cases/bad_* trees must fail and one good_* tree must pass.
        D-038 (DECISIONS §F.7, UNREVIEWED, in the review queue) records it, and
        D-019 gains a note that its reasoning still holds.
WHY:    The old grep banned `socket` outside src/interface/, so the Unix sockets
        B.2, D-042 and D-043 need in the supervisor, storaged and analyzed would
        fail `make test` and invite weakening the check (CLAUDE.md §2.8); its
        curl_ and SSL_ patterns could never match; and it ignored connect paths,
        address families, headers, include/ and the link line (board item
        `boundaryrule`, #171; handout §10.3).
REVIEW: The three grep patterns in check.sh are the rule; read them against the
        eight cases. It is a text check, so a comment naming a banned call fails
        the build: the safe direction.
VERIFY: check.sh --selftest tests/boundary/cases: exit 0 (each bad_* case reports
        its violation, good_* passes); check.sh . on the real tree: PASS;
        make test: boundary PASS and all tests PASS.

####
# CI for the systems core (CLAUDE.md §1): a change is done only when make, make test and
# make asan pass. This runs them with gcc and glibc on 64-bit Arm Linux, the Pi's
# architecture, so a Mac-only build (Apple clang) is never the only evidence.
#
# valgrind (make memcheck) and anything that needs the car or the adapter stay on the Pi.
####
name: build

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  core:
    name: make, make test, make asan (gcc, arm64 Linux)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: make
        run: make
      - name: make test
        run: make test
      - name: make asan
        run: make asan

input.content:
## What this changes

This makes the build gates trustworthy and adds Linux CI.

- `make asan` builds in its own tree, so a plain `make` after it links again.
- `make test` (and therefore `make asan`) compiles every daemon.
- A UBSan finding now fails instead of printing PASS.
- The scripts the Makefile and docs run are executable.
- `make memcheck` explains itself when valgrind is missing.
- `make deploy` stops copying the venv, raw drive data, soak logs and transcripts.
- The Python probe tests the version, not `tomllib`.
- The boundary check is rewritten and tests itself (D-038).
- The analysis requirements install on Python 3.11, the Pi's version.
- A CI job runs `make`, `make test` and `make asan` with gcc on arm64 Linux.

**Branched from `camden/m2/stale-refs` (#179), itself on #167: merge those first.**

## Why

CLAUDE.md §1 defines "done" as `make`, `make test` and `make asan` passing, and the
audit found each of them gave weaker evidence than it appeared to:

- `make` failed after `make asan`;
- no daemon was ever sanitized;
- UBSan could not fail a test;
- the boundary check could not match curl or SSL and would have rejected the Unix
  sockets the design needs;
- nothing ever built on Linux.

Handout §13 caps a component at 50 % on sanitizer findings, and §10.3 makes the boundary
check the grader's 60-second proof.

Closes #170
Closes #171
Closes #172

**Decision IDs touched:** D-038 (new, UNREVIEWED); note on D-019
**Milestone:** M2
**Mechanism affected (D / E / none):** none directly; it gates both

## Review this hardest

- `tests/boundary/check.sh`: the three grep patterns are the rule, and the eight cases
  under `tests/boundary/cases/` are its tests. A rule that stops matching now fails the
  self-test.
- The `asan` target: `BUILD=$(BUILD)/asan` relies on make's command-line variable
  override reaching every derived path (`BIN`, `COMMON_OBJ`, `TEST_BIN`).

## What I am least sure about

- The 3.11 pins (matplotlib 3.10.9, numpy 2.4.6) were checked for wheel availability,
  not installed on a 3.11 machine; the CI job is the first real install.
- The CI job is new; if it is red, the failure tells us something the Mac could not
  (gcc warnings, LeakSanitizer).

## Commit-by-commit

1. M2 build: build the sanitizer variant in build/asan so plain make still links
2. M2 build: make test build every daemon, so make asan sanitizes them too
3. M2 build: make a UBSan finding fail the asan run instead of printing PASS
4. M2 build: mark the scripts the Makefile and docs run directly as executable
5. M2 build: say where to run memcheck when valgrind is missing
6. M2 build: keep the venv, raw drive data, soak logs and transcripts out of deploy
7. M2 build: pick Python by version, not by tomllib, and drop the dead CC line
8. M2 build: let the boundary check allow Unix sockets and test itself, as D-038
9. M2 tools: pin matplotlib and numpy per Python version, so 3.11 can install them
10. M2 build: run make, make test and make asan in CI with gcc on arm64 Linux
11. M2 process: correct board.yml's rule citation and its expired soft-launch date

input.description: Fix Python tool bugs on branch
input.prompt:
You are fixing audited bugs in the Python tools of a CS370 student project (carwatch: an in-car Raspberry Pi that reads engine sensors from an OBDLink LX Bluetooth OBD2 adapter via ELM327/STN commands). You work in an isolated git worktree of the repo (originally at /Users/crash/dev/school/cs370/car-watch). This is Camden's session.

## Setup
1. In your worktree, create branch `camden/m2/tool-fixes` from the current HEAD, which must be branch `camden/m2/build-gates` (commit 76a304e or later). Verify with `git log --oneline -1`. If HEAD is not build-gates, `git switch -c camden/m2/tool-fixes camden/m2/build-gates`.
2. Read CLAUDE.md fully first and obey it. Key rules for you: never commit to main; never push; never open/merge PRs; never run `python tools/board_sync.py` without `--check`/`--status` (it mutates GitHub); never `git add -A`/`.`/`commit -a` — stage explicit paths; never commit a file whose full current contents you have not read; one commit = one responsibility (state it in one sentence without "and"); tests ship in the same commit as the behavior; never weaken/skip/delete a test; commit message format is `.gitmessage` (`M2 tools: <imperative summary>` then WHAT/WHY/REVIEW/VERIFY lines, wrapped ~76 cols) and every message ends with a blank line then `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Write commit messages to a file with your file-writing tool and use `git commit -F file` in a SEPARATE command (do not chain a heredoc after `&&` — a failed check before it still lets the commit run with a stale message; that bug already happened once this session).
3. Before each commit: run the Python tests `PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests/tools -q` (the venv is at the original repo path /Users/crash/dev/school/cs370/car-watch/.venv if your worktree has none — use that interpreter) and `python3 tools/test_board.py`, plus the linters on every touched file: markdownlint `/Users/crash/.npm/_npx/3c2a9ea6c4b6e0a2/node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli2 <md files>` and cSpell `/Users/crash/.npm/_npx/b338be11c6678430/node_modules/.bin/cspell --no-progress --no-summary <files>` (run from the worktree root so `cspell.json` and `.markdownlint.jsonc` apply). Add genuine new words to cspell.json (keep its list sorted case-insensitively, JSON indent 2) in the commit that introduces them. Do NOT run `make asan` concurrently with anything (it is fine to run `make test` in your worktree at the end, once).
4. Do not touch: src/, include/, Makefile, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/milestones.md, partners/, tests/*.c, tests/boundary/. Another session is editing C code in parallel.

## Fix list (from a read-only audit; verify each against the code before changing it — if a finding is wrong, skip it and say so)
Each numbered item is its own commit unless two are genuinely one responsibility. Each behavior change ships with a unittest in tests/tools/ that fails before the fix (say so in VERIFY).

board_sync.py (board item `toolfix`, #173):
1. Lines ~368-375/394: tags for newly created issues are written back to docs/milestones.md only at the very end; a gh failure or Ctrl-C after a create leaves the file unwritten and the next run creates duplicate issues. Write the file after each successful create/tick (or in a finally whenever at least one write happened). Test with a mocked gh runner.
2. Lines ~202-209: `read_json(..., default=[])` turns gh read failures (network, auth) into empty results, so sync tries to create milestones/reports issues missing; make issue and milestone reads raise on failure (keep the soft default only for the project-board read). Test.
3. Lines ~154-167: `render` rewrites every `| M[0-6] |` row anywhere in the file, not only inside the `<!-- board-sync:milestones -->` markers. Scope it. Test with a fixture that has such a row elsewhere.
4. Lines ~270-282: an edit label prints only `--title`; print old -> new title so a mis-tagged line that would retitle another issue is visible in --check. Test.
5. board_sync.py:25 says "Python 3.11+" for tomllib, which is no longer imported: fix the stale comment (separate small commit, or fold into whichever board_sync commit touches that area only if it is the same responsibility — otherwise separate).

elm.py / obdlib.py:
6. elm.py ~49-62: after a Timeout, the next command() resets the input buffer and writes immediately while the adapter may still be answering the old request, so a late reply can be taken as the next answer (wrong data, wrong time) or the ELM prints STOPPED. After a timeout, send "\r" and drain until the ">" prompt (bounded wait) before the next command. Test with obdsim or a fake serial.
7. elm.py ~71 init(): `UNABLE TO CONNECT` / `CAN ERROR` (bus asleep, key off) currently loop as AdapterError -> reinit storm in obdlog. Treat them as "bus asleep" (a distinct exception or NoData-like path) and back off in obdlog. Test.
8. elm.py ~78-89 supported_pids(): NO DATA from a later block (0120/0140...) raises and aborts setup; catch it and stop the chain. Test.
9. obdlib.py ~20-24: add the real texts `BUS INIT: ...ERROR` / `BUS INIT: ...OK` to the right lists (cosmetic; small commit with a test).

obdlog.py:
10. ~52, ~222: the file name is stamped to the second and opened with "a"; two sessions in one second append into one file. Open with "x" and add milliseconds (and/or pid) to the name. Test.
11. ~62-66: `rec.update(fields)` lets fields override `src`, `type`, `seq`; make those reserved (raise or drop with an assertion). Integrity rule CLAUDE.md §2.7. Test.
12. ~108-113: a second Ctrl-C cannot abort a blocked open; on the second signal raise KeyboardInterrupt (the finally still writes the footer). Test if feasible without real signals flakiness; otherwise a unit test of the handler logic.
13. ~345: any unexpected exception writes footer reason "link_gave_up"; record `error: <type>: <msg>` instead. Test.
14. ~218, ~276: validate --pids before connecting; reject an empty PID list (all([]) is True so the loop idles forever). Test.
15. ~332: GPS is polled only after a successful sample; poll it while every PID is absent too (respect the existing 2 Hz cap). Test.
16. ~209: the header stores socket.gethostname() (privacy; D-033 does not list it). Drop it. Update any test that asserted it — that is a deliberate change, say so in its own commit's WHY (CLAUDE.md §2.8: never weaken a test silently).

New decision D-044 (record it in docs/DECISIONS.md as a new entry `### C.8 — Drive logs keep every answering ECU's line and poll rpm and load more often (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED` in section C after C.7, with the fields used by neighbouring entries: `D-044` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜, sections Decision (draft) / Why / Cost / Alternative rejected; and add a review-queue row in the table at the top, keeping that table sorted by ID — D-044 goes after D-043), implemented in the SAME commit(s) as its code:
17. With ATH0, when several ECUs answer one Mode 01 request (ECM and TCM often both answer 0C, 0D, 05), elm/obdlib take the first line, so samples may silently mix ECUs. Do NOT switch to headers on (ATH1) — the header formats differ by protocol and nothing has been measured on the real cars yet (CLAUDE.md §8.4). Instead: keep every answering line, record `n_ecu` (how many lines answered) and all raw lines in the sample record, decode the first as today, and emit a `multi_ecu` event the first time a PID gets more than one answer. Filtering by ECU is decided after the first drive's evidence. Tests with obdsim (extend obdsim to optionally answer some PIDs from two ECUs, labeled synth).
18. Scheduling: rpm (0C) and load (04) are binning axes, but round-robin over ~30 PIDs refreshes them only every 1.5–3 s, beyond obdbins' 1.5 s freshness window. Poll 0C and 04 every 4th request (configurable `--fast`, default "0C,04", `--fast ""` disables), and read static PIDs (01 monitor status excluded — it carries the MIL bit, keep polling it slowly; but 1C OBD standard, 51 fuel type, 13/1D O2 locations) once at start into the header instead of every pass. Record the schedule in the header. D-044 covers this too; it amends D-033's "every supported PID round-robin". Tests.

Viewers:
19. obdplot.py ~80: crashes with ValueError when there are no decoded samples (all NO DATA). Fix and test.
20. obdplot.py ~69 vs ~33, obdview.py ~150: events use t0 = first record of any kind, series use t0 = first decoded sample; share one t0. Test.
21. obdview.py ~154, obdplot.py ~43, obdbins.py ~57 read `src` from the first record only; reuse obdsum's all-records check (refuse mixed src). Test.

Docs:
22. tools/pidscan.py docstring says `data/pidscan-<time>.json`; actual is `pidscan-<time>-<src>.json`. Fix.
23. tools/requirements-gps.txt: pin pyobjc-framework-CoreLocation to the version currently installed if it is installed in the venv (`.venv/bin/pip show`); if not installed, leave it unpinned and say why in the final report (do not install anything).
24. If D-044 changes what docs/hardware/first-drive.md or tools/README.md say (e.g. new flags), update them in the same commit as the behavior.

## When done
- Run `make test` once in your worktree (not make asan) and paste its tail.
- Do NOT push. Leave all commits on branch `camden/m2/tool-fixes`.
- Final report: the branch name and HEAD hash, one line per commit (hash + subject), any audit finding you skipped and why, anything you were unsure about, and the verbatim tail of the final test run.

10. ~52, ~222: the file name is stamped to the second and opened with "a"; two sessions in one second append into one file. Open with "x" and add milliseconds (and/or pid) to the name. Test.
11. ~62-66: `rec.update(fields)` lets fields override `src`, `type`, `seq`; make those reserved (raise or drop with an assertion). Integrity rule CLAUDE.md §2.7. Test.
12. ~108-113: a second Ctrl-C cannot abort a blocked open; on the second signal raise KeyboardInterrupt (the finally still writes the footer). Test if feasible without real signals flakiness; otherwise a unit test of the handler logic.
13. ~345: any unexpected exception writes footer reason "link_gave_up"; record `error: <type>: <msg>` instead. Test.
14. ~218, ~276: validate --pids before connecting; reject an empty PID list (all([]) is True so the loop idles forever). Test.
15. ~332: GPS is polled only after a successful sample; poll it while every PID is absent too (respect the existing 2 Hz cap). Test.
16. ~209: the header stores socket.gethostname() (privacy; D-033 does not list it). Drop it. Update any test that asserted it — that is a deliberate change, say so in its own commit's WHY (CLAUDE.md §2.8: never weaken a test silently).

New decision D-044 (record it in docs/DECISIONS.md as a new entry `### C.8 — Drive logs keep every answering ECU's line and poll rpm and load more often (draft) ⚠️ UNREVIEWED` in section C after C.7, with the fields used by neighbouring entries: `D-044` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜, sections Decision (draft) / Why / Cost / Alternative rejected; and add a review-queue row in the table at the top, keeping that table sorted by ID — D-044 goes after D-043), implemented in the SAME commit(s) as its code:
17. With ATH0, when several ECUs answer one Mode 01 request (ECM and TCM often both answer 0C, 0D, 05), elm/obdlib take the first line, so samples may silently mix ECUs. Do NOT switch to headers on (ATH1) — the header formats differ by protocol and nothing has been measured on the real cars yet (CLAUDE.md §8.4). Instead: keep every answering line, record `n_ecu` (how many lines answered) and all raw lines in the sample record, decode the first as today, and emit a `multi_ecu` event the first time a PID gets more than one answer. Filtering by ECU is decided after the first drive's evidence. Tests with obdsim (extend obdsim to optionally answer some PIDs from two ECUs, labeled synth).
18. Scheduling: rpm (0C) and load (04) are binning axes, but round-robin over ~30 PIDs refreshes them only every 1.5–3 s, beyond obdbins' 1.5 s freshness window. Poll 0C and 04 every 4th request (configurable `--fast`, default "0C,04", `--fast ""` disables), and read static PIDs (01 monitor status excluded — it carries the MIL bit, keep polling it slowly; but 1C OBD standard, 51 fuel type, 13/1D O2 locations) once at start into the header instead of every pass. Record the schedule in the header. D-044 covers this too; it amends D-033's "every supported PID round-robin". Tests.

Viewers:
19. obdplot.py ~80: crashes with ValueError when there are no decoded samples (all NO DATA). Fix and test.
20. obdplot.py ~69 vs ~33, obdview.py ~150: events use t0 = first record of any kind, series use t0 = first decoded sample; share one t0. Test.
21. obdview.py ~154, obdplot.py ~43, obdbins.py ~57 read `src` from the first record only; reuse obdsum's all-records check (refuse mixed src). Test.

Docs:
22. tools/pidscan.py docstring says `data/pidscan-<time>.json`; actual is `pidscan-<time>-<src>.json`. Fix.
23. tools/requirements-gps.txt: pin pyobjc-framework-CoreLocation to the version currently installed if it is installed in the venv (`.venv/bin/pip show`); if not installed, leave it unpinned and say why in the final report (do not install anything).
24. If D-044 changes what docs/hardware/first-drive.md or tools/README.md say (e.g. new flags), update them in the same commit as the behavior.

## When done
- Run `make test` once in your worktree (not make asan) and paste its tail.
- Do NOT push. Leave all commits on branch `camden/m2/tool-fixes`.
- Final report: the branch name and HEAD hash, one line per commit (hash + subject), any audit finding you skipped and why, anything you were unsure about, and the verbatim tail of the final test run.

"""elm: one serial session with an ELM327-compatible adapter, run against obdsim."""
import os
import tempfile
import time
import unittest

import elm
import obdsim


class AgainstSim(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.link = os.path.join(self.dir.name, "obd")
        self.srv = obdsim.PtyServer(link=self.link, latency=0.0).__enter__()
        self.ad = elm.Adapter(self.link)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.ad.close()
        self.srv.__exit__(None, None, None)
        self.dir.cleanup()

    def test_init_returns_the_banner_and_flags_a_simulator(self):
        banner = self.ad.init()
        self.assertIn("ELM327", banner)
        self.assertTrue(self.ad.is_sim)

    def test_query_returns_data_bytes(self):
        self.ad.init()
        self.assertEqual(len(self.ad.query(1, 0x0C)), 2)

    def test_supported_pids_walks_the_chain(self):
        self.ad.init()
        self.assertEqual(self.ad.supported_pids(), set(obdsim.MODELED))

    def test_protocol_voltage_and_vin(self):
        self.ad.init()
        self.assertIn("15765", self.ad.protocol())
        self.assertRegex(self.ad.voltage(), r"V$")
        self.assertEqual(self.ad.vin(), obdsim.SIM_VIN)

    def test_a_reply_returns_as_soon_as_its_prompt_arrives(self):
        self.ad.init()
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        for _ in range(40):
            self.ad.query(1, 0x0C)
        self.assertLess(time.monotonic() - t0, 1.0, "40 queries to a zero-latency sim")

    def test_link_lost_when_the_port_goes_away(self):
        self.ad.init()
        self.srv.__exit__(None, None, None)
        with self.assertRaises((elm.LinkLost, elm.Timeout)):
            for _ in range(3):
                self.ad.query(1, 0x0C)
        self.srv = obdsim.PtyServer(link=self.link, latency=0.0).__enter__()


class Opening(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_missing_port_is_link_lost(self):
        with self.assertRaises(elm.LinkLost):

M2 tools: report a port that vanished on Linux as a lost link, not a crash

WHAT:   elm.Adapter.command() also turns termios.error into LinkLost; the error
        tuple is PORT_ERRORS, with termios imported only where it exists.
WHY:    The new Linux CI job showed test_link_lost_when_the_port_goes_away
        erroring: on Linux, flushing a tty whose other end has gone raises
        termios.error (EIO), which is not an OSError, so a Bluetooth drop on the
        Pi would have escaped as an unhandled exception instead of the
        `link_lost` and reconnect that DESIGN §4 promises. macOS never raised it.
REVIEW: The obdsim EBADF in the same CI log was a knock-on: the failed assertion
        skipped the test's re-creation of the simulator, so tearDown closed it
        twice. It disappears with this fix, so obdsim is unchanged.
VERIFY: tests/tools on macOS: 91 tests OK; the CI job on this branch is the Linux
        check.

M3 store: make the CRC32 table a constant, removing its first-use race

WHAT:   src/store/crc32.c holds the 256-entry table as a static const array
        instead of building it on first call behind a plain int flag;
        tests/test_crc32.c checks the table against the bitwise CRC definition
        for lengths 0 to 256 and onward to 1024. Its comment now cites CLAUDE.md
        §8.6 (smallest diff), not §7.6.
WHY:    Two threads making the first call could both build the table while one
        reads it, a data race and so undefined behavior; storaged will CRC from
        more than one path (writes and recovery). A constant table needs no
        initialization at all.
REVIEW: The table was generated by script and is trusted only because the new
        test recomputes every entry's effect bit by bit; the known-answer test
        (0xCBF43926) is unchanged.
VERIFY: make test PASS (test_crc32 PASS); make asan PASS.

/* On-disk record format — mechanism D.
 *
 * The constraint: power disappears every time the key turns off. The box shuts down
 * cleanly when its supercapacitor allows (D-024), but a cold-start crank, a pulled
 * cable or an empty bank can still cut a write, so the format must let recovery find
 * the torn tail and truncate it without losing anything before it.
 *
 * Therefore every record is (a) self-framing, so a scan can resynchronize, and
 * (b) CRC'd over its whole body, so a partially-flushed record is detectable rather
 * than merely wrong. Records are written in committed batches (D-025): a batch with
 * no COMMIT on disk is discarded at recovery.
 */
#ifndef CARWATCH_RECORD_H
#define CARWATCH_RECORD_H

#include <stdint.h>

#define REC_MAGIC   0x43574B31u   /* "CWK1" */
#define REC_VERSION 1u

typedef struct {
    uint32_t magic;      /* REC_MAGIC — resync anchor for the recovery scan */
    uint16_t version;
    uint16_t len;        /* bytes of payload following this header */
    uint64_t seq;        /* monotonic; a gap here is a detected loss, not a hidden one */
    uint64_t mono_ns;    /* CLOCK_MONOTONIC — for intervals, survives wall-clock jumps */
    uint64_t wall_ns;    /* CLOCK_REALTIME, set from the RTC at boot (D-030); untrusted if
                          * the RTC reported invalid time */
    uint8_t  src;        /* data_src_t — live | replay | synth. Never optional. */
    uint8_t  kind;       /* rec_kind_t */
    uint16_t _pad;
    uint32_t crc32;      /* over header-with-crc-zeroed, then payload */
} rec_hdr_t;

typedef enum {
    REC_OBD_RAW    = 1,   /* raw adapter reply line, kept for replay (D-015) */
    REC_SAMPLE     = 2,   /* decoded PID sample */
    REC_BASELINE   = 3,   /* persisted per-bin statistics — must survive power loss */
    REC_VERDICT    = 4,
    REC_FAULT      = 5,   /* detection / degradation / recovery event */
    REC_HEARTBEAT  = 6
} rec_kind_t;

uint32_t rec_crc32(const void *buf, uint32_t len);

#endif

M3 store: replace the record sketch with D-034's format and a checked codec

WHAT:   include/store/record.h now defines D-034's layout: magic "CWR1", a
        40-byte little-endian header (kind, body_len, seq, mono_ns, wall_ns, src,
        flags, boot_id), six body kinds (sample, begin, commit, boot, shutdown,
        event), the D-037 box-sensor namespace, and a trailing CRC32, with static
        asserts on every size and offset, byte order and float width.
        src/store/record.c adds rec_encode and rec_decode; tests/test_record.c
        round-trips every kind, flips every bit of a sample record, cuts it at
        every length, and checks the encoder refuses what the decoder rejects.
        storaged's start line logs the format instead of the removed REC_VERSION.
WHY:    The old sketch (magic "CWK1", a version field, the CRC inside the header,
        kinds OBD_RAW to HEARTBEAT) contradicted D-034, and its kind numbers meant
        different things (2 was SAMPLE, D-034's BEGIN). storaged and its recovery
        (`storewrite`, `storerecover`) need one codec that never accepts a damaged
        or partial record.
REVIEW: rec_decode's order of checks: magic, kind, body_len, then SHORT, then CRC,
        then src and the event's inner length. A torn tail must read as SHORT or
        BAD_CRC and never as valid; the flip and cut tests are that proof. A
        CRC-valid record with src 0 is reported as BAD_SRC, a writer bug.
VERIFY: make test: test_record PASS (with test_crc32, test_ring, boundary,
        toolcheck); make asan: all PASS.

input.content:
M3 ipc: read the ring's tail before its head so no observer sees a negative depth

WHAT:   ring_depth loads tail, then head. test_ring.c gains a concurrent test: a
        producer thread, the main thread consuming 400,000 slots, and an observer
        thread calling ring_depth throughout; it checks order, payloads and that
        no observed depth exceeds RING_CAPACITY.

        the single-threaded tests never did. The audit reproduced it 915 times in
        one run.
REVIEW: The argument in the comment: head is monotonic, so any head read after a
        tail read is at least that tail.

        capacity") and passes after, three runs in a row; make test PASS; make
        asan PASS.

input.content:
M3 ipc: initialize the ring's atomics properly and require them lock-free

WHAT:   ring_init zeroes only the slots and sets head, tail and overruns with
        atomic_init instead of memset over the atomics followed by stores; ring.c
        asserts at compile time that 64-bit atomics are always lock-free.
WHY:    memset on an _Atomic object is not a defined way to initialize it. And the
        ring is about to be shared between processes: a 64-bit atomic that is not
        lock-free (possible on a 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS) falls back to a lock held
        in one process's memory, which protects nothing across two.
REVIEW: The assert makes a 32-bit build fail loudly rather than run unsafely;
        provisioning will require the 64-bit OS.
VERIFY: make test: test_ring PASS; make asan PASS (arm64 macOS:
        ATOMIC_LLONG_LOCK_FREE == 2; Linux CI checks gcc on arm64).

entry="""### B.12 — The rings live in shared memory the supervisor creates; `storaged` frees a slot only after `fsync` ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-039` · Decided M3, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Extends:** 🔒 B.3 (refuse, never overwrite), whose rule is unchanged; D-031 and
D-037 (one producer and one consumer per ring) · **Answers:** board item `ringshm`

**Decision.**

- **Peek, then release.** The consumer reads slots with `ring_peek` and frees them with
  `ring_release(n)`. `storaged` releases a batch's slots only after that batch's
  `COMMIT` has been `fsync`'d, so a `kill -9` of `storaged` before then loses nothing:
  the restarted `storaged` finds the same slots still in the ring.
- **The ring numbers its slots.** `ring_push` sets each slot's `seq` from the ring's own
  head, so numbering survives a producer restart and a gap is a real loss.
- **Lifecycle.** The supervisor creates each ring at start with `shm_open` and `mmap`
  (`ring_create`), removing a stale object left by a previous boot first. `obdd`,
  `ambientd` and `storaged` attach to it (`ring_attach`), which checks a header (magic,
  layout version, capacity, slot size) and refuses an object written by a different
  build. Only the creator initializes; a restarted child attaches and never resets the
  indices the other side is using.
- **Duplicates after a restart.** If `storaged` dies after `fsync` returns but before the
  release, the restarted process sees that batch again. Recovery knows the last committed
  sample's `mono_ns` for each ring in the current boot, and `storaged` skips ring slots
  at or before it, so a batch is never written twice.

**Why.** With `ring_pop`, a slot left the ring the moment `storaged` read it, up to a
second before it was durable (D-035), so killing `storaged` (the soak's injected fault,
mechanism E's test) silently lost those samples, the loss B.3 exists to prevent. A
shared-memory ring that any child re-initializes on restart would reset the other side's
indices; a header check stops a ring left over from an older build being read with a new
layout.

**Cost.** A ring holds at most 4096 slots, about 200 s at 20 samples a second, so a
`storaged` that is down longer makes the producer refuse (counted, B.3). The duplicate
rule relies on `mono_ns` growing within a boot, which `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` guarantees.

"""

  (`ring_create`), removing a stale object left by a previous boot first. `obdd`,
  `ambientd` and `storaged` attach to it (`ring_attach`), which checks a header (magic,
  layout version, capacity, slot size) and refuses an object written by a different
  build. Only the creator initializes; a restarted child attaches and never resets the
  indices the other side is using.
- **Duplicates after a restart.** If `storaged` dies after `fsync` returns but before the
  release, the restarted process sees that batch again. Recovery knows the last committed
  sample's `mono_ns` for each ring in the current boot, and `storaged` skips ring slots
  at or before it, so a batch is never written twice.

**Why.** With `ring_pop`, a slot left the ring the moment `storaged` read it, up to a
second before it was durable (D-035), so killing `storaged` (the soak's injected fault,
mechanism E's test) silently lost those samples, the loss B.3 exists to prevent. A
shared-memory ring that any child re-initializes on restart would reset the other side's
indices; a header check stops a ring left over from an older build being read with a new
layout.

**Cost.** A ring holds at most 4096 slots, about 200 s at 20 samples a second, so a
`storaged` that is down longer makes the producer refuse (counted, B.3). The duplicate
rule relies on `mono_ns` growing within a boot, which `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` guarantees.

M3 store: write batches durably and recover the committed prefix after any cut

WHAT:   New include/store/wal.h and src/store/wal.c: storaged's write-ahead log.
        wal_add buffers records in a batch opened by BEGIN; wal_due says when it
        holds 64 samples or is a second old (D-035); wal_commit appends COMMIT,
        writes the batch, fsyncs, and on any failure cuts the file back to its
        last commit and reports it so the caller keeps its ring slots. Segments
        are log-<first seq>.cwr, rotated at 16 MB, with the directory fsync'd on
        create (D-034). wal_open scans the newest segment (wal_scan), truncates
        everything after the last COMMIT, and commits a boot record saying
        whether the last session ended clean or was recovered, with the bytes
        truncated and samples lost (D-025). wal_close commits a SHUTDOWN batch.
        tests/test_wal.c writes, reopens, and cuts a 3,692-byte log at every byte
        offset: the scan must keep exactly the batches committed before the cut,
        and every 13th cut also runs the real open on the cut file.
WHY:    Board items `storewrite` (#39) and `storerecover` (#40): the core of
        mechanism D. The writer and the recovery are one commit because wal_open
        always recovers before it writes, and the cut test needs the writer to
        build the logs it cuts; about 600 lines for that reason.
REVIEW: wal_scan's rules: every record must sit inside BEGIN..COMMIT, a COMMIT
        must name its BEGIN's txn, and the first record that fails to decode ends
        the scan. wal_commit's undo path. What it does not do yet: retention
        (D-041), the event socket (D-042), and the per-ring duplicate skip after a
        restart (D-039), which come with the storaged daemon.
VERIFY: make test: test_wal PASS (every one of 3,693 cuts, about 285 real opens);
        make asan: test_wal PASS.

input.content:
M3 ipc: stamp each ring with a generation so a fresh ring is never mistaken for an old one

WHAT:   ring_t's header gains `generation`, set once by ring_create from the wall
        clock and the creator's pid; RING_VERSION goes to 3. test_shm.c checks a
        re-created ring gets a new, non-zero generation.
WHY:    D-039 has a restarted storaged skip ring slots at or before the last
        sample it committed, by mono_ns. That is right after storaged alone
        restarts, but after a reboot the supervisor makes a fresh ring whose
        mono_ns starts near zero, and skipping by an old mono_ns would drop real
        samples. storaged will record each ring's generation in its log and skip
        only when the generation matches.
REVIEW: A generation only has to differ between creations, not be secret: two
        creations in the same nanosecond by the same pid cannot happen. If the
        clock read fails it is logged and the value is still the pid's.
VERIFY: make test: test_shm PASS; make asan PASS.

WHAT:   ring_t's header gains `generation`, set once by ring_create from the wall
        clock and the creator's pid; RING_VERSION goes to 3. test_shm.c checks a
        re-created ring gets a new, non-zero generation.
WHY:    D-039 has a restarted storaged skip ring slots at or before the last
        sample it committed, by mono_ns. That is right after storaged alone
        restarts, but after a reboot the supervisor makes a fresh ring whose
        mono_ns starts near zero, and skipping by an old mono_ns would drop real
        samples. storaged will record each ring's generation in its log and skip
        only when the generation matches.
REVIEW: A generation only has to differ between creations, not be secret: two
        creations in the same nanosecond by the same pid cannot happen. If the
        clock read fails it is logged and the value is still the pid's.
VERIFY: make test: test_shm PASS; make asan PASS.

M3 store: write batches durably and recover the committed prefix after any cut

WHAT:   New include/store/wal.h and src/store/wal.c: storaged's write-ahead log.
        wal_add buffers records in a batch opened by BEGIN; wal_due says when it
        holds 64 samples or is a second old (D-035); wal_commit appends COMMIT,
        writes the batch, fsyncs, and on any failure cuts the file back to its
        last commit and reports it so the caller keeps its ring slots. Segments
        are log-<first seq>.cwr, rotated at 16 MB, with the directory fsync'd on
        create (D-034). wal_open scans the newest segment (wal_scan), truncates
        everything after the last COMMIT, and commits a boot record saying
        whether the last session ended clean or was recovered, with the bytes
        truncated and samples lost (D-025). wal_close commits a SHUTDOWN batch.
        tests/test_wal.c writes, reopens, and cuts a 3,692-byte log at every byte
        offset: the scan must keep exactly the batches committed before the cut,
        and every 13th cut also runs the real open on the cut file.
WHY:    Board items `storewrite` (#39) and `storerecover` (#40): the core of
        mechanism D. The writer and the recovery are one commit because wal_open
        always recovers before it writes, and the cut test needs the writer to
        build the logs it cuts; about 600 lines for that reason.
REVIEW: wal_scan's rules: every record must sit inside BEGIN..COMMIT, a COMMIT
        must name its BEGIN's txn, and the first record that fails to decode ends
        the scan. wal_commit's undo path. What it does not do yet: retention
        (D-041), the event socket (D-042), and the per-ring duplicate skip after a
        restart (D-039), which come with the storaged daemon.
VERIFY: make test: test_wal PASS (every one of 3,693 cuts, about 285 real opens);
        make asan: test_wal PASS.

input.content:
## What this changes

This is the storage half of the M3 pipeline: mechanism D, plus the shared-memory handoff
mechanism E needs.

- **Record format.** D-034 is implemented as a checked codec. Its tests flip every bit
  and cut every length of a record; no damaged or partial record ever decodes.
- **Shared-memory ring.**
  - It lives in shared memory that the supervisor creates and children attach to,
    checked by a header and a generation stamp.
  - The consumer peeks, then releases a slot only after it is durable (D-039).
  - The ring numbers its own slots and refuses unlabeled ones (D-040).
  - Fixed bugs: an underflowing `ring_depth`, false sharing, and `memset` on atomics.
- **The write-ahead log.** Batches are BEGIN, samples, COMMIT, then one `fsync` at 64
  samples or one second; segments rotate at 16 MB. Recovery keeps exactly the committed
  prefix and writes a boot record saying whether the last session ended clean. It is
  tested by cutting a real log at every one of its 3,693 byte offsets.
- **`storaged`, a real daemon.** It drains both rings into the log. A test runs the
  real binary: 1,000 samples, `kill -9` after 300, a restart, then `SIGTERM`. The log
  holds all 1,000 exactly once and ends clean.

**Branched from `camden/m2/tool-fixes`, on #180, #179 and #167: merge those first.**

## Why

The M3 exit criterion is "sensors through the real pipeline into real storage; one
menu mechanism working" (handout §6, §13). Mechanism D's measurement is "write batching
and `fsync` discipline; recovery after a mid-write power cut" (§3.2). The every-byte cut
test is the hardware-free form of that, and the `kill -9` test is mechanism E's promise
that a dying child loses nothing.

Closes #38
Closes #39
Closes #40

**Decision IDs touched:** D-039 and D-040 (new, UNREVIEWED); D-034 amended (src
encoding); implements D-025, D-034, D-035
**Milestone:** M3
**Mechanism affected (D / E / none):** D (storage) and E (the cross-process ring)

## Review this hardest

- `src/ipc/ring.c`: the memory ordering in `ring_peek` and `ring_release` (acquire on
  head, release on tail).
- `src/store/wal.c`, `wal_scan`: the rules that decide what recovery keeps.
- `src/store/main.c`: the order "note ring seq, commit, then release", and what a
  failed commit does.

## What I am least sure about

- `fsync` on macOS does not reach stable storage (`F_FULLFSYNC` does). The cut test
  proves the logic, not the SD card. The Pi's `expcrash` is still the real test.
- The first draft skipped duplicates by `mono_ns`; the restart test caught it losing a
  sample, and it now uses ring `seq`. D-039's text says so.
- Not yet built on this path: the event socket (D-042, waiting on the supervisor),
  retention (D-041), and the durable offset `analyzed` will read (D-031).

## Commit-by-commit

1. M3 store: make the CRC32 table a constant, removing its first-use race
2. M3 common: make a src of zero mean unlabeled, never live, as D-040
3. M3 store: replace the record sketch with D-034's format and a checked codec
4. M3 ipc: read the ring's tail before its head so no observer sees a negative depth
5. M3 ipc: give the ring's head, tail and counter a cache line each
6. M3 ipc: initialize the ring's atomics properly and require them lock-free

mechanism E needs.

- **Record format.** D-034 is implemented as a checked codec. Its tests flip every bit
  and cut every length of a record; no damaged or partial record ever decodes.
- **Shared-memory ring.**

    checked by a header and a generation stamp.
  - The consumer peeks, then releases a slot only after it is durable (D-039).
  - The ring numbers its own slots and refuses unlabeled ones (D-040).
  - Fixed bugs: an underflowing `ring_depth`, false sharing, and `memset` on atomics.
- **The write-ahead log.** Batches are BEGIN, samples, COMMIT, then one `fsync` at 64
  samples or one second; segments rotate at 16 MB. Recovery keeps exactly the committed
  prefix and writes a boot record saying whether the last session ended clean. It is
  tested by cutting a real log at every one of its 3,693 byte offsets.

  real binary: 1,000 samples, `kill -9` after 300, a restart, then `SIGTERM`. The log
  holds all 1,000 exactly once and ends clean.

## What this changes

This fixes the bugs the 2026-10-26 audit found in the Python tools, before the first
real drive depends on them. Every behavior change ships with a test that failed against
the old code.

- **`board_sync`**
  - Writes each new issue's tag back as soon as the issue exists, so a failure or Ctrl-C
    mid-sync can no longer create duplicate issues.
  - Stops when it cannot read issues or milestones, instead of treating the failure as
    an empty board.
  - Only touches the marked table.
  - Shows old to new titles.
- **The adapter session (`elm`)**
  - Waits out a timed-out reply before the next request, so a late answer is never
    taken as the next one.
  - Treats `UNABLE TO CONNECT` and `CAN ERROR` as a sleeping bus. Before the fix, 1.5 s
    with the key off meant 8,712 adapter resets.
  - Ends the PID walk at an empty block.
  - Knows the `BUS INIT` texts.
- **`obdlog`**
  - One file per session, stamped to the millisecond.
  - `src` and the stamps cannot be overwritten.
  - A second Ctrl-C stops it at once.
  - The footer names the real error.
  - The PID list is checked before connecting.
  - GPS keeps logging while the engine is silent.
  - No hostname in the header.
- **D-044 (draft).** Keep every answering ECU's line instead of silently mixing two
  ECUs. Poll rpm and load every fourth request so binning sees fresh values. Read static
  PIDs once. Headers stay off until a real car is measured.
- **Viewers**
  - `obdplot` no longer crashes with no decoded samples.
  - Events and series share one time zero.
  - Every viewer refuses a log with mixed `src`.

**Branched from `camden/m2/build-gates` (#180), on #179 and #167: merge those first.**

## Why

The first Forester drive (`firstcap`, `pidforester`) runs on these tools, and several
bugs would have cost data or integrity in the car: wrong-ECU readings, a reset storm
with the key off, two sessions appended into one file, and a `src` a field could
overwrite (CLAUDE.md §2.7).

Closes #173

**Decision IDs touched:** D-044 (new, UNREVIEWED), amending D-033
**Milestone:** M2
**Mechanism affected (D / E / none):** none (tools only)

## Review this hardest

- Commit 18 changes the shape of the `obdlog` loop: one PID per iteration instead of one
  pass. Every error branch keeps its behavior.
- Commit 6, the resync after a timeout: `RESYNC_WAIT` is 0.5 s, unmeasured on the LX.
  A bare CR is sent only when no late prompt arrives, because a CR to an idle ELM327
  repeats the last command.

## What I am least sure about

- `CAN ERROR` is treated as a sleeping bus. The datasheet also lists wiring faults as a
  cause; on a real car that would show as `bus_asleep` with no `bus_awake`.
- In commit 17, four `obdlog` tests that mocked `Adapter.query` now mock `query_all`
  with the same failures. Nothing is weakened; the commit message says so.
- Written by a Claude subagent in Camden's session and checked by the parent session
  with `make`, `make test` and `make asan`. Read it with that in mind.

**Decision (draft).** `data_src_t` and the record's `src` byte are 1 `live`, 2 `replay`,
3 `synth`. Zero is `SRC_INVALID`: a record, ring slot or log line carrying it is
rejected, never stored, and `log_src_name` prints `invalid`.

**Why.** With `live` as zero, any slot or record built from zeroed memory, or by code that
forgot to set the field, was labeled live without anyone choosing that label, and
`tests/test_ring.c` was already pushing unlabeled test data that way. C.2 makes `src`
mandatory precisely so the label cannot be forgotten; a zero that means `live` undoes
that. Moving the values now costs nothing, because no record has been written yet.

**Cost.** Every producer must set `src` explicitly, which is the point. The obdlog JSONL
files (D-033) use strings, not these numbers, so they are unaffected.

+### B.12 — The rings live in shared memory the supervisor creates; `storaged` frees a slot only after `fsync` ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
+`D-039` · Decided M3, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
+· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
+· **Extends:** 🔒 B.3 (refuse, never overwrite), whose rule is unchanged; D-031 and
+D-037 (one producer and one consumer per ring) · **Answers:** board item `ringshm`
+**Decision.**
+- **Peek, then release.** The consumer reads slots with `ring_peek` and frees them with
+  `ring_release(n)`. `storaged` releases a batch's slots only after that batch's
+  `COMMIT` has been `fsync`'d, so a `kill -9` of `storaged` before then loses nothing:
+  the restarted `storaged` finds the same slots still in the ring.
+- **The ring numbers its slots.** `ring_push` sets each slot's `seq` from the ring's own
+  head, so numbering survives a producer restart and a gap is a real loss.
+- **Lifecycle.** The supervisor creates each ring at start with `shm_open` and `mmap`
+  (`ring_create`), removing a stale object left by a previous boot first. `obdd`,
+  `ambientd` and `storaged` attach to it (`ring_attach`), which checks a header (magic,
+  layout version, capacity, slot size) and refuses an object written by a different
+  build. Only the creator initializes; a restarted child attaches and never resets the
+  indices the other side is using.
+- **Duplicates after a restart.** If `storaged` dies after `fsync` returns but before the
+  release, the restarted process sees that batch again. So every batch also records, as
+  an event, the `seq` of the newest ring slot it holds, and each run records which ring
+  instance it drains (its generation, set at creation). After a restart, `storaged` skips
+  slots at or below the last committed ring `seq`, but only for the same ring instance:
+  a ring made fresh at the next boot is never skipped. A batch is never written twice.
+**Why.** With `ring_pop`, a slot left the ring the moment `storaged` read it, up to a
+second before it was durable (D-035), so killing `storaged` (the soak's injected fault,
+mechanism E's test) silently lost those samples, the loss B.3 exists to prevent. A
+shared-memory ring that any child re-initializes on restart would reset the other side's
+indices; a header check stops a ring left over from an older build being read with a new
+layout.
+**Cost.** A ring holds at most 4096 slots, about 200 s at 20 samples a second, so a
+`storaged` that is down longer makes the producer refuse (counted, B.3). Two small events
+per batch (the ring generation once per run, the newest ring `seq` per batch). A first
+draft skipped by `mono_ns` instead; the restart test lost a sample to two readings with
+the same timestamp, which ring `seq` cannot have.

| Merge order | PR | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [#167](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/167) | Puts the design doc on `main` (#166 had landed on the wrong branch). Adds the DS18B20 probe (D-037) and drafts the open design holes (D-041 retention, D-042 event path, D-043 query protocol and `obdctl` verbs). Completes the evaluation plan. DESIGN.md renders to 5 pages. |
| 2 | [#179](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/179) | Removes every stale reference across the docs, freezes REVISION_PLAN.md as history, and adds board lines for the gaps nothing tracked. |
| 3 | [#180](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/180) | Build fixes: `make` works after `make asan`; the daemons are sanitized; UBSan findings now fail; the network boundary check is rewritten and tests itself (D-038). Adds the Linux CI job. |
| 4 | [#181](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/181) | 22 Python tool fixes before the first drive, plus D-044 (keep every answering ECU's line; poll rpm and load more often). |
| 5 | [#182](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/182) | The storage half of M3. Covers the record format, the shared-memory ring (D-039, D-040) and the write-ahead log, and makes `storaged` a real daemon. |

**Things worth knowing:**
- **Two tests now back mechanism D.** One cuts a real log at every byte offset and checks recovery keeps exactly the committed batches. The other runs the real `storaged`, kills it with `kill -9` mid-stream and restarts it: 1,000 samples land exactly once. That test caught a lost sample in my first version, which I fixed by matching restarts on the ring's sequence numbers instead of timestamps.

# CS370 Term Project — Team Rules

**Project:** `carwatch`, an in-vehicle diagnostic recorder, on whenever the car is, that
learns *this* car's normal and reports developing faults before a check-engine light would.
**Team:** Camden Thomas (`crash8750@gmail.com`) · Lance Baron · CS 370, Colorado State
(Pallickara). **Rubric:** `docs/handout/CS370-TermProject.md`; the rubric is law, and this
file is how we obey it.

> **Read this file every session.** It holds the rules only, short enough to load every
> time. Everything else has exactly one home: **`docs/README.md`** maps each topic to its
> source doc. Rationale for the rules below is in `docs/PROCESS.md`.

## 0. Every session

You (Claude) are required in our **workflow** and forbidden in our **product** (handout
§3.3, §10.3).

**Start:**

1. Read `docs/milestones.md` (where we are), then the review queue at the top of
   `docs/DECISIONS.md` (what is settled, what awaits review).
2. `python tools/board_sync.py --status`. Pick work from the open boxes in
   `docs/milestones.md`, nowhere else.
3. State whose session this is (Camden's or Lance's), for transcripts and attribution.
   Any open task may be taken (D-026); do not edit a subsystem the other partner has
   claimed (§6) without being told.
4. `git status` clean, `git pull` on `main`, create the branch **before** the first edit.

**End, every time:**

1. Nothing uncommitted, no stray files.
2. PR opened or updated as a draft, template filled, `make` / `make test` / `make asan`
   output pasted.
3. Every decision made without a human present is in `docs/DECISIONS.md` as ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
   and in its review queue, **in the same commit that implements it**.
4. `python tools/board_sync.py`, the only thing that moves cards.
5. Copy this session's `.jsonl` out (`partners/<name>/transcripts/README.md`).
6. Print a summary: branch, one line per commit, PR link, decisions added, and what
   specifically needs human review.

Never reopen a 🔒 LOCKED decision without saying so and getting a human yes. **Claude
never marks a decision reviewed or LOCKED**; only Camden or Lance does, in their own commit.

## 1. Commands

```sh
make              # build everything, -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
make test         # unit tests + boundary check + milestones.md check
make asan         # tests under AddressSanitizer + UBSan
make memcheck     # valgrind over the test binaries
make soakcheck    # 1-hour miniature of the 48h run
make hwcheck      # KiCad ERC; violations fail the build
make hwdocs       # regenerate schematic SVG, BOM and netlist
make replay FIX=fixtures/<name>   # a labeled capture through the real pipeline
make deploy PI=pi@<host>          # rsync + remote build
python tools/board_sync.py --status | --check | (no flag = reconcile)
```

**A change is DONE only when `make`, `make test` and `make asan` all pass and the output
is pasted.** Not "should pass." Output.

## 2. Hard constraints (graded boundaries)

1. **No hosted models in the product.** No LLM API calls, no cloud inference, no network
   calls of any kind except serving its own LAN interface. A grader must confirm this in
   sixty seconds by reading the tree. `src/` contains no HTTP client. Ever.
2. **Our model, our weights.** Classifier trained by us, on our data, training code in
   `tools/train/`, weights versioned in `models/`. No third-party pretrained weights.
   Inference is C we wrote.
3. **The device works with the network unplugged.** Full stop.
4. **Systems core is C17**, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, no VLAs, `goto`-cleanup for
   multi-resource functions. Every allocation checked. Every syscall error path handled
   *and logged*.
5. **Python lives only in `tools/` and `ui/`.** No graded mechanism may hide there.
6. **Every daemon is supervisable:** clean exit codes, no orphaned fds across restart,
   heartbeat within 60 s of start, survives `kill -9` of any sibling.
7. **Replayed or synthesized data is labeled as such EVERYWHERE**: every record carries
   `src=live|replay|synth`. Integrity boundary, not a style choice.
8. **Never weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.** If a test is wrong,
   say so and fix it deliberately, in its own commit, with the reason.

## 3. What we are building

A Raspberry Pi in a car. The testbeds are Camden's **2008 Subaru Forester** and Lance's
**2015 Honda CR-V EX-L**, and neither is required of anyone (D-022). A Bluetooth
Classic OBD2 adapter in the OBD2 port is read over RFCOMM as `/dev/obd` (D-019). The Pi
lives in one small box with one USB-C port, fed by the owner's own charger, and a
seconds-scale supercapacitor lets it shut down cleanly at key-off; it is off while the car
is, and nothing is cut (D-024). Mode 01 requests (D-012) read every engine sensor
the car publishes; the device learns *this car's* normal per operating point, flags what
leaves it, and names the likely fault area. A rough first draft, not a finished product.
The owner reads it on a phone over the device's own Wi-Fi (D-013) or with `obdctl`; one
tri-color light pulses while on duty (D-027).

**The claim we defend (D-021, D-022):** *"learns the normal of the car it is installed in
across its engine sensors, flags behavior outside it and names the likely fault area, with
measured catch and false-alarm rates on faults we induce."* Not "predicts failure"
(handout §5).

## 4. Mechanisms

Committed and measured: **D** (append-only, crash-consistent storage) and **E**
(multi-process with a supervisor). **B** and **F** are declined: no Pi-side sensor

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The product boundary (CLAUDE.md §2.1, D-038): a grader must confirm in sixty seconds that
# the only network code is the box's own page server. This is that confirmation.
#
#   check.sh ROOT                 check ROOT/src, ROOT/include and ROOT/Makefile
#   check.sh --selftest CASES     every CASES/bad_* must fail and every CASES/good_* pass
#
# The rules, applied to *.c and *.h, comments included:
#   1. No network family, resolver or address call outside src/interface/.
#   2. No HTTP or TLS library, no Bluetooth socket header, and no shelling out, anywhere.
#   3. socket() only in src/ipc/uds.c (Unix sockets, D-042, D-043) and src/interface/.
#   4. The Makefile links no network library.
set -uo pipefail

check() {
    local root=$1 bad=0 hits
    local dirs=()
    for d in src include; do [[ -d "$root/$d" ]] && dirs+=("$root/$d"); done

    scan() {  # scan PATTERN -> "file:line:text" for every C file under src/ and include/
        [[ ${#dirs[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0
        grep -rnE --include='*.c' --include='*.h' "$1" "${dirs[@]}" 2>/dev/null
    }
    report() {  # report RULE HITS
        [[ -z "$2" ]] && return 0
        printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed "s|^$root/||; s|^|  $1: |"
        bad=1
    }

    hits=$(scan '\b(AF|PF)_(INET6?|PACKET|NETLINK)\b|\b(getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|gethostbyaddr|getnameinfo|inet_(pton|ntop|addr|aton|ntoa))\b|#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(netdb\.h|netinet/|arpa/inet\.h)' \
           | grep -v "^$root/src/interface/")
    report "network outside src/interface/" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(curl/|openssl/|bluetooth/)|\b(curl_[a-z]|SSL_[A-Za-z])|\bAF_BLUETOOTH\b|\b(popen|system)[[:space:]]*\(')
    report "HTTP, TLS, Bluetooth socket or shell" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '\bsocket(pair)?[[:space:]]*\(' \
           | grep -v -e "^$root/src/interface/" -e "^$root/src/ipc/uds\.c:")
    report "socket() outside src/ipc/uds.c and src/interface/" "$hits"

    if [[ -f "$root/Makefile" ]]; then
        hits=$(grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(LDLIBS|LDFLAGS).*-l(curl|ssl|crypto|bluetooth)\b' "$root/Makefile" \
               | sed 's|^|Makefile:|')
        report "network library linked" "$hits"
    fi
    return $bad
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--selftest" ]]; then
    cases=${2:?usage: check.sh --selftest CASES}
    fail=0
    for c in "$cases"/bad_* "$cases"/good_*; do
        name=$(basename "$c")
        if check "$c" >/dev/null; then got=pass; else got=fail; fi
        case "$name:$got" in
            bad_*:fail|good_*:pass) ;;
            *) echo "boundary self-test: $name should not $got"; fail=1 ;;
        esac
    done
    exit $fail
fi

root=${1:?usage: check.sh ROOT | --selftest CASES}
if ! check "$root"; then
    echo "BOUNDARY VIOLATION: see CLAUDE.md §2.1 and DECISIONS D-038"
    exit 1
fi
